jobs.descriptionHtml:
🧠 About Legion Health

At Legion Health, we believe everyone deserves fast, affordable, and world-class health care, and we’re developing the AI infrastructure to deliver it ourselves at world scale.

Legion is building autonomous medical care (the AI doctor), starting with psychiatry. Our AI-native care-delivery platform currently automates 95% of the administrative work required for us to deliver direct patient care. We also recently became the first company ever to receive regulatory authorization to let AI prescribe psychiatric medications, allowing us to not only collapse health care’s admin costs but also its clinical labor costs—shifting this industry’s economics from humans to tokens.

Our technical moat is hard to copy—we combine rich data, production AI, doctors in the loop, and end-to-end care operations to deliver measurably better care to a clinically complex patient population. This has helped us produce tens of thousands of total visits in just 2 years, all while holding ops costs flat and achieving industry-leading patient NPS and retention. While the last generation of healthcare startups made the existing system incrementally more efficient, Legion is rebuilding full-stack care delivery from first principles. Our vision? A 10X better patient experience that’s higher quality, less expensive, and more scalable than ever before. And a 10X better clinician experience that frees our providers to focus on what matters most: caring for patients.

Legion Health is backed by Y Combinator, leading venture capital firms, and founders from Function Health, Modern Health, Everly Health, Trusted Health, Clipboard Health, PatientPing, Sesame Care, Faire, EasyPost, and fuboTV.

Join us as we build the future of health care: faster, higher-quality, and more affordable, powered by doctors and AI working together.

📍 Role Logistics

  • Job Type: Full-Time

  • Role Type: Product / Technical Product Management / Consumer AI / Patient Experience / Retention

  • Ideal Experience Level: 5+ years

  • Location: San Francisco

  • US Visa Sponsorship: Yes

🚀 The Opportunity

Legion is hiring a Founding Product Manager, Consumer + AI to own the consumer product experience that turns AI-native care delivery into something patients can understand, trust, use, and return to.

This is not a technical program management role, an enterprise roadmap coordinator role, or a “growth PM” role with healthcare language added on top. You will own real product surface area across Legion’s patient journey: onboarding, intake, eligibility, scheduling, visit prep, provider matching, care-plan clarity, medication workflows, follow-up, renewals, messaging, reactivation, and the moments that make a patient feel safe enough to come back.

The right person is technical enough to reason through APIs, data models, event instrumentation, AI workflows, edge cases, system constraints, and engineering tradeoffs, but consumer-minded enough to know that the best product often feels obvious, calm, and human. You should be able to sit with a patient problem, map the underlying clinical and operational workflow, write a crisp product spec, prototype the interaction, instrument the funnel, partner deeply with engineering and design, ship the feature, and decide whether it actually improved care.

Legion is a modern consumer AI software company that happens to deliver medical care. That means the product bar is closer to Anthropic, OpenAI, Character.AI, Replit, Oura, WHOOP, Duolingo, Chime, Monarch, and the best consumer health companies than to traditional healthcare software. We need someone who can bring that level of product taste, technical speed, and retention thinking into a regulated, high-trust category where quality and safety matter.

This is a high-ownership IC role with founder-level visibility and a direct path to Head of Product. You will work directly with engineering, design, clinical, operations, growth, data, compliance, and the founders to turn messy real-world care delivery into simple, powerful product experiences.

✅ Responsibilities and Deliverables

  • Own core patient-facing product surfaces across the full consumer journey: discovery, onboarding, intake, insurance/payment clarity, scheduling, provider fit, visit prep, visit completion, follow-up, care-plan adherence, refills, renewals, messaging, support, retention, and reactivation.

  • Translate complex clinical, operational, regulatory, and AI workflows into simple consumer experiences that reduce anxiety, increase clarity, and help patients know exactly what to do next.

  • Build durable product systems, not one-off features: patient timeline, care status, tasking, reminders, notifications, escalation paths, asynchronous messaging, support deflection, eligibility logic, provider availability, and follow-up workflows.

  • Partner with engineering to scope and ship technically sound products across web, mobile-responsive experiences, backend workflows, APIs, third-party integrations, event pipelines, data models, and AI-assisted workflows.

  • Define and own product metrics for your surface area, including activation, intake completion, scheduling conversion, first-visit completion, time to care, repeat-visit rate, renewal completion, retention, NPS/CSAT, patient confusion, support burden, no-shows, and ops cost per visit.

  • Use PostHog, SQL, analytics tools, customer support data, operational dashboards, and qualitative research to identify patient friction, prioritize product bets, and measure whether shipped work moved the right metrics.

  • Design and run structured experiments where appropriate, while knowing when a healthcare product needs principled product judgment, clinical input, and quality thresholds instead of pure A/B testing.

  • Own product specs, user stories, acceptance criteria, rollout plans, QA checklists, experiment plans, metric definitions, launch notes, and post-launch readouts with enough clarity that engineering, clinical, ops, and growth can all execute cleanly.

  • Prototype quickly using Figma, v0, Lovable, Replit, Cursor, Codex, Claude Code, lightweight scripts, no-code tools, or whatever helps you make product ideas concrete before engineering invests real cycles.

  • Ship production PRs regularly. This is a product role—not a software-engineering role—but you are expected to work directly in the codebase and open production-quality PRs for well-scoped changes such as instrumentation, internal tools, workflow logic, UI and copy improvements, prototypes, and small fixes. You should be comfortable testing, reviewing, and safely rolling out your work in close partnership with engineering.

  • Partner with clinical and operations teams to deeply understand real patient and provider workflows, including edge cases: missed appointments, medication refill timing, insurance confusion, state/provider availability, pharmacies, clinical escalations, patient safety concerns, handoffs, and support loops.

  • Partner with compliance, legal, privacy, and clinical leadership to design AI-enabled product experiences with appropriate safeguards, human review, auditability, expectation-setting, and patient trust.

  • Improve Legion’s AI product layer: patient-facing AI interactions, AI-assisted intake, personalization, care navigation, workflow automation, internal copilots, clinical/ops review queues, and evaluation loops that make automation safer and more useful over time.

  • Create product feedback loops from patient conversations, support tickets, provider feedback, drop-off data, session recordings, funnel analytics, and clinical/ops metrics so the roadmap is grounded in real behavior, not vibes.

  • Work with growth and brand to ensure acquisition promises match the actual product experience, so the patients we bring in understand what Legion does, feel properly oriented, and are more likely to stay in care.

  • Raise the product craft bar across Legion: clearer flows, better defaults, fewer dead ends, tighter copy, sharper state handling, cleaner mobile experiences, stronger instrumentation, faster iteration, and more rigorous launch quality.

🏆 You’ll Be Successful If You…

  • Make Legion’s patient experience feel consumer-grade: fast, clear, calm, trustworthy, and easy to return to.

  • Improve the core retention loop of care: more patients complete intake, make it to their first visit, understand the next step, follow through on care plans, complete renewals when eligible, and come back when they need help.

  • Turn messy clinical and operational workflows into product systems that scale without making patients feel like they are navigating a maze.

  • Ship AI-enabled experiences that feel useful and safe, with clear boundaries around what AI does, what doctors do, and when humans review or intervene.

  • Build a measurement system that makes the patient journey legible: every meaningful step has an owner, a metric, and a path to improvement.

  • Reduce patient confusion and support burden by improving the product itself, not just by adding more manual operations.

  • Help Legion move faster without becoming sloppy: strong specs, smart scoping, crisp decisions, high-quality launches, and honest post-launch learning.

  • Earn trust from engineering because you understand technical constraints and tradeoffs, and from clinical/ops teams because you understand the reality of care delivery.

  • Create product experiences that are emotionally intelligent without being soft, technically sophisticated without being confusing, and ambitious without being reckless.

  • Help build the product foundation for a company that can deliver world-class medical care at dramatically lower cost.

🧰 Ideal Background and Skills

  • 5+ years of product management, product engineering, technical founder, or equivalent experience, with meaningful ownership of consumer-facing web or mobile products.

  • Strong consumer product instincts. You have shipped products that people actually use, understand, trust, and return to, not just internal tools or enterprise workflows.

  • Technical fluency across software product development. You can reason through APIs, data models, event instrumentation, backend workflows, frontend states, AI workflows, latency, failure modes, privacy constraints, and engineering tradeoffs.

  • Hands-on technical curiosity. You can navigate API docs, logs, event payloads, session recordings, agent traces, and enough of a codebase to understand what is really happening without pulling engineers into every first-pass investigation.

  • Experience partnering deeply with engineering and design from problem definition through launch: discovery, PRDs/specs, UX flows, technical scoping, sprint planning, QA, rollout, metric tracking, and iteration.

  • Strong analytical ability. You are comfortable with SQL or equivalent data exploration, product analytics tools such as PostHog, Amplitude, Mixpanel, Looker, Hex, or Mode, and you can define useful metrics without waiting for someone else to hand you a dashboard.

  • Track record improving engagement, retention, activation, conversion, habit formation, lifecycle, or core experience metrics in a consumer product.

  • High product taste and UX judgment. You care about copy, information architecture, interaction design, empty states, error states, mobile responsiveness, notification timing, trust cues, and the emotional texture of the user experience.

  • AI-native working style. You already use tools like Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Replit, Lovable, v0, ChatGPT, Claude, Figma AI, or similar tools to prototype, analyze, write, synthesize, debug, and move faster.

  • Comfort working on AI-enabled products where the PM must think about prompt behavior, user expectations, evaluation, quality thresholds, fallback paths, human review, auditability, and safety.

  • Healthcare experience is a strong plus but not required. Experience in another trust-sensitive consumer category such as fintech, insurance, family/kids, identity, privacy, marketplaces, wellness, or regulated consumer products is also valuable.

  • Startup operating mode: high agency, low ego, high urgency, strong writing, strong judgment, strong follow-through. You can create clarity without waiting for a perfect org chart.

  • Ability to work cross-functionally with clinical, operations, support, compliance, legal, growth, data, design, engineering, and founders without losing the thread of the user problem.

  • Excellent writing. You can write crisp strategy docs, product specs, launch plans, decision memos, patient-facing copy, and post-launch analyses.

  • Bias toward building. You are happiest when you are close to the product, close to users, close to the data, and shipping.

  • Bonus: experience at or near companies like Anthropic, OpenAI, Character.AI, Replit, Cursor, Perplexity, Notion, Duolingo, Oura, WHOOP, Chime, Monarch Money, Rocket Money, Acorns, Function Health, Nourish, General Medicine, Circle Medical, Tava Health, Headway, Rula, Midi Health, Evvy, Ro, Hims & Hers, Thirty Madison, Levels, Superpower, or another breakout consumer product with high craft, high trust, and fast iteration.

💰 Compensation & Benefits

  • Salary: $190,000 – $290,000

  • Early-Stage Equity: Meaningful ownership in a category-defining company.

  • Health Insurance: Medical, dental, and vision benefits

  • Additional Perks: In-person retreats, meal stipends, AI/product tooling budget, learning stipend, home office support

  • Time Off: Flexible, unlimited vacation policy

  • Work Hours: Flexible

  • Work Setup: In-person in San Francisco

  • Impact: Build the product layer for a company trying to change health care forever.

  • Autonomy and Learning: Own major patient-facing product surfaces end-to-end, from product strategy through technical scoping, launch, measurement, and iteration.

  • Growth Opportunities: As we scale, this role can grow into Staff Product Manager, Product Lead, or Head of Product scope.

📝 How to Apply and Hiring Process

  • Apply here: https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/legionhealth/0ffded39-1242-4a35-9bc3-0e5b0ce22276

  • Overview of our hiring process:

    1. Resume + Application Screen

    2. Founder / Product Interview

    3. Technical Product Deep Dive

    4. Cross-Functional Interviews with Engineering, Design, Clinical/Ops, Growth, and Founders

    5. Professional Reference Checks

  • Estimated time-to-hire: 2 weeks

  • Start date: ASAP

  • Hiring manager: Arthur MacWaters

🤝 Equal Employment Opportunity

Legion Health is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees, contractors, and applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or any other protected characteristic under applicable law. We encourage applicants from all backgrounds to apply.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
🧠 About Legion Health

At Legion Health, we believe everyone deserves fast, affordable, and world-class health care, and we’re developing the AI infrastructure to deliver it ourselves at world scale.

Legion is building autonomous medical care (the AI doctor), starting with psychiatry. Our AI-native care-delivery platform currently automates 95% of the administrative work required for us to deliver direct patient care. We also recently became the first company ever to receive regulatory authorization to let AI prescribe psychiatric medications, allowing us to not only collapse health care’s admin costs but also its clinical labor costs—shifting this industry’s economics from humans to tokens.

Our technical moat is hard to copy—we combine rich data, production AI, doctors in the loop, and end-to-end care operations to deliver measurably better care to a clinically complex patient population. This has helped us produce tens of thousands of total visits in just 2 years, all while holding ops costs flat and achieving industry-leading patient NPS and retention. While the last generation of healthcare startups made the existing system incrementally more efficient, Legion is rebuilding full-stack care delivery from first principles. Our vision? A 10X better patient experience that’s higher quality, less expensive, and more scalable than ever before. And a 10X better clinician experience that frees our providers to focus on what matters most: caring for patients.

Legion Health is backed by Y Combinator, leading venture capital firms, and founders from Function Health, Modern Health, Everly Health, Trusted Health, Clipboard Health, PatientPing, Sesame Care, Faire, EasyPost, and fuboTV.

Join us as we build the future of health care: faster, higher-quality, and more affordable, powered by doctors and AI working together.

📍 Role Logistics

  • Job Type: Full-Time

  • Role Type: People / Talent / Recruiting / People Operations

  • Ideal Experience Level: 5+ years

  • Location: San Francisco

  • Work Setup: In person in San Francisco; this is not a remote role

  • Reports To: Co-founder and CEO

  • US Visa Sponsorship: Yes

🚀 The Opportunity

Legion is hiring a Head of Talent and People to build the talent engine and people operating system behind a category-defining healthcare company.

You will be the senior-most owner of People and Talent at Legion. You will own the entire employee journey—from the first outbound recruiting message through interviews, closing, relocation, onboarding, performance, development, compensation, engagement, and eventual offboarding.

This is an unusually broad, hands-on leadership role. In the same week, you might personally source an exceptional AI engineer, close a senior operator, coach a manager through difficult feedback, review payroll, coordinate an employee’s move to San Francisco, improve onboarding, and produce a company dinner or offsite.

You will not inherit a large recruiting or HR team. During the first 12–18 months, you are the team: the lead recruiter, People operator, culture builder, employee-experience owner, and trusted adviser to the founders. You will build systems and eventually hire support only where the company’s scale and bottlenecks justify it.

The right person combines the talent instincts of an elite startup recruiter, the operational precision of an exceptional People leader, the judgment of a trusted executive partner, and the warmth of someone who genuinely enjoys creating an extraordinary place to work.

This is not a role for someone who wants to advise from a distance, manage a team of recruiters, or hand execution to vendors. We need a player-coach who can build the strategy, open Ashby, source candidates, close offers, fix broken processes, and personally make sure every new employee has a laptop and a great first day.

✅ Responsibilities and Deliverables

  • Own Legion’s company-wide talent plan: translate business priorities, product roadmaps, clinical expansion, and organizational constraints into a sequenced hiring plan with clear role priorities, scorecards, timelines, and accountable hiring managers.

  • Personally run full-cycle recruiting across AI and engineering, product, consumer growth, operations, finance, clinical leadership, executive, and other hard-to-fill roles—from role kickoff and sourcing through assessment, references, offer negotiation, and close.

  • Build exceptional outbound pipelines. Identify and engage high-performing passive candidates through targeted research, personalized outreach, referrals, communities, events, founder networks, and persistent relationship-building.

  • Create a rigorous hiring standard for every role: outcome-based scorecards, calibrated interview plans, structured questions, useful work samples, interviewer training, evidence-based debriefs, references, and explicit hiring decisions.

  • Become a compelling closer. Understand what motivates each candidate and thoughtfully navigate compensation, equity, risk, mission, career trajectory, immigration, relocation, counteroffers, family considerations, and other barriers to joining an early-stage company.

  • Deliver an unusually strong candidate experience: fast communication, organized scheduling, prepared interviewers, honest expectations, thoughtful selling, clear decisions, and respectful rejection.

  • Build Legion’s employer brand and talent narrative across job descriptions, recruiting content, founder channels, employee stories, events, referrals, candidate materials, and targeted communities.

  • Own recruiting operations and analytics, including Ashby configuration, pipeline integrity, scheduling workflows, templates, agency management, recruiting spend, weekly talent reviews, forecasting, and hiring-manager accountability.

  • Measure recruiting performance using metrics that matter: quality of hire, source quality, qualified pipeline, conversion by stage, time in stage, time to fill, offer acceptance, hiring-manager responsiveness, candidate experience, retention, and agency dependence.

  • Own the complete employee lifecycle: offers, employment agreements, background checks, work authorization, onboarding, employee records, status changes, leaves, promotions, compensation changes, transfers, departures, and offboarding.

  • Run reliable payroll and payment operations for employees and contractors. Coordinate payroll changes, bonuses, deductions, reimbursements, commissions where applicable, tax registrations, and issue resolution accurately and on time.

  • Own the operating relationship with benefits, payroll, HRIS, equity, immigration, background-check, employment-law, and other People vendors. Hold every partner accountable for service, accuracy, cost, and employee experience.

  • Administer and continuously improve medical, dental, vision, leave, retirement, wellness, and other benefit programs, ensuring employees understand and can actually use what Legion provides.

  • Partner with finance and leadership on compensation philosophy, salary bands, equity practices, offer construction, promotions, market calibration, headcount planning, and People budgets.

  • Build pragmatic People infrastructure: policies, handbook, compliance calendar, employee files, required notices, training, reporting, approval workflows, templates, manager resources, and a clear source of truth.

  • Coordinate with qualified employment, immigration, benefits, tax, and other counsel to manage California and multi-state employment requirements, worker classification, accommodations, leaves, investigations, immigration, terminations, and other sensitive matters. You are not expected to be Legion’s lawyer, but you are accountable for recognizing risk early and getting the right advice.

  • Handle employee relations with discretion, fairness, speed, and sound judgment. Support investigations, performance concerns, interpersonal conflict, accommodations, conduct issues, improvement plans, and departures without avoiding difficult decisions.

  • Build a high-quality performance system: clear expectations, direct feedback, regular check-ins, talent reviews, manager calibration, development plans, promotion decisions, recognition, and decisive intervention when performance falls below Legion’s standard.

  • Help leadership design the organization as it scales: roles, reporting lines, spans of control, responsibilities, decision rights, succession risk, management capacity, and where the company should hire, develop, redesign, or part ways.

  • Coach founders and managers to become exceptional talent leaders. Help them set expectations, give feedback, interview effectively, make difficult calls, recognize excellent work, and build teams with high talent density.

  • Own relocation to San Francisco for new and existing employees. Design the policy and coordinate immigration, travel, temporary housing, moving support, reimbursements, payroll and state transitions, family considerations, and local onboarding from signed offer through successful arrival.

  • Make every employee operationally ready on Day 1. Coordinate laptops, accessories, mobile-device management, software, email, permissions, security access, account provisioning, workspace, onboarding schedules, equipment inventory, replacements, and returns.

  • Build an onboarding experience that accelerates time to impact: preboarding, company context, role-specific plans, compliance and security training, manager preparation, introductions, 30/60/90-day expectations, and structured feedback.

  • Own the San Francisco employee and workplace experience, including office operations, meals, supplies, vendors, workspace readiness, candidate onsite visits, safety, and the details that allow the team to do excellent work.

  • Create memorable internal experiences: team dinners, celebrations, launches, traditions, learning sessions, retreats, offsites, community events, and other moments that make Legion demanding, energizing, and fun.

  • Own the operating details behind company events, including objectives, budgets, venues, travel, vendors, accessibility, communications, attendance, execution, and post-event feedback.

  • Build effective internal communications so employees understand company priorities, organizational changes, new hires, policies, decisions, expectations, and the reasoning behind them.

  • Listen to the organization without becoming governed by surveys or consensus. Use direct conversations, employee feedback, manager input, operating data, and judgment to identify risks and improve the employee experience.

  • Use AI aggressively and responsibly to improve sourcing, outreach, scheduling, documentation, onboarding, employee self-service, People analytics, knowledge management, and repetitive administration while protecting confidential employee and candidate information.

  • Build the People and Talent team over time. Hire recruiters, coordinators, People operators, workplace support, or specialist partners only when the data and organizational needs justify additional leverage.

🏆 You’ll Be Successful If You…

  • Within your first 30 days, you understand Legion’s business, team, open roles, hiring constraints, compensation practices, People systems, vendors, organizational risks, and most urgent operational gaps.

  • Every priority opening has a clear scorecard, calibrated interview process, accountable hiring manager, sourcing strategy, recruiting owner, and realistic closing plan.

  • Within 90 days, Legion has consistent outbound pipelines for its hardest roles, a disciplined weekly talent review, reliable recruiting data, and substantially less founder time lost to scheduling and recruiting administration.

  • Candidates move through Legion’s process quickly, encounter prepared interviewers, receive clear communication, and leave with a stronger impression of the company regardless of the final decision.

  • Legion consistently hires unusually capable people rather than merely filling seats. Quality of hire and long-term talent density remain more important than raw hiring volume.

  • Offers close because candidates understand Legion’s mission, expectations, upside, risks, compensation, equity, working environment, and the extraordinary opportunity in front of them.

  • Every new hire arrives in San Francisco with relocation barriers addressed and begins Day 1 with the necessary equipment, access, schedule, context, relationships, and expectations.

  • Payroll, benefits, employee records, compliance deadlines, equity coordination, equipment, onboarding, and offboarding operate reliably without recurring surprises or manual heroics.

  • Managers give clearer feedback, address performance problems earlier, interview more effectively, and make better organizational decisions because of your coaching and systems.

  • Legion develops a practical compensation, leveling, performance, and promotion framework that employees and managers can understand without creating unnecessary bureaucracy.

  • Company events and rituals strengthen trust, connection, energy, and shared purpose rather than feeling like obligatory corporate programming.

  • You identify organizational, compliance, employee-relations, and retention risks before they become crises, and leadership trusts you to handle sensitive situations with discretion and courage.

  • You build a People function that is highly responsive and deeply human while remaining operationally rigorous, analytically grounded, and appropriately lean.

  • AI and automation eliminate meaningful administrative work without degrading candidate experience, employee trust, data security, or decision quality.

  • Twelve months from now, Legion has measurably higher talent density, a more predictable recruiting engine, stronger managers, faster onboarding, clearer expectations, and substantially less reactive People work sitting with the founders.

🧰 Ideal Background and Skills

  • 5+ years of progressively responsible experience spanning recruiting, talent leadership, People Operations, HR, or organizational leadership at high-growth technology companies.

  • Experience serving as the first, early, or senior-most People and Talent hire at a venture-backed startup—ideally while scaling from approximately 25–50 employees to 100–150+.

  • Demonstrated success personally sourcing, assessing, and closing exceptional passive candidates for difficult roles. You are still energized by recruiting and do not consider sourcing or coordination beneath your level.

  • Strong technical-recruiting ability across AI, engineering, data, and product, plus the versatility to recruit consumer growth, operations, clinical leadership, finance, and executive talent.

  • Evidence that your hires became high-performing, durable members of the organization—not simply that you hit an annual hiring number.

  • Experience building recruiting infrastructure from zero or rebuilding an inconsistent system: workforce planning, scorecards, structured interviews, interviewer training, referrals, sourcing operations, analytics, employer branding, and closing.

  • Hands-on People Operations experience across payroll, benefits, HRIS, employee records, equity administration, onboarding, offboarding, leaves, policies, vendor management, and compliance.

  • Sound working knowledge of California and multi-state employment practices, with the judgment to identify when specialized employment, immigration, tax, or benefits counsel is required.

  • Experience managing sensitive employee-relations matters, investigations, performance improvement, terminations, accommodations, organizational changes, and other high-stakes situations.

  • Experience designing or operating compensation bands, leveling, performance reviews, promotion processes, talent reviews, manager training, and workforce planning.

  • Excellent judgment under ambiguity. You can balance speed, consistency, empathy, legal risk, individual circumstances, and company standards without hiding behind policy.

  • Strong analytical fluency. You can build dashboards, diagnose funnel problems, forecast hiring capacity, audit compensation, evaluate vendors, and distinguish useful People data from vanity metrics.

  • Comfortable with tools such as Ashby, Rippling, Gusto, Justworks, Deel, Carta, Pave, Slack, Notion, Google Workspace, modern device-management systems, and AI tools for sourcing, analysis, automation, and documentation.

  • Exceptional written and verbal communication. You can write a compelling outbound message, a precise policy, a sensitive employee communication, a strong job description, and a clear executive recommendation.

  • High discretion and unquestioned integrity. People trust you with information that cannot be mishandled, politicized, or casually shared.

  • High warmth and high standards. You care deeply about people without confusing care with avoiding accountability or lowering the bar.

  • Strong hospitality and event instincts. You notice the operational details that make interviews, first days, dinners, retreats, and the everyday workplace feel intentional.

  • Low ego, high urgency, and founder-level ownership. You can set a talent strategy Monday, source candidates Tuesday, fix payroll Wednesday, coach a manager Thursday, and run an exceptional team event Friday.

  • Willing and excited to work in person in San Francisco and to help build an in-person culture with exceptional energy, trust, and execution.

  • Especially valuable: Experience in healthcare, regulated technology, AI, clinician recruiting, mixed employee/contractor workforces, immigration, relocation, workplace operations, or rapid office-based scaling.

💰 Compensation & Benefits

  • Salary: $170,000–$260,000, based on experience

  • Early-Stage Equity: Meaningful ownership in a category-defining company

  • Health Insurance: Medical, dental, and vision benefits

  • Relocation: Support for moving to San Francisco

  • US Visa Sponsorship: Available for exceptional candidates

  • Additional Perks: In-person retreats, company events, meal stipends, AI tooling, and professional-development support

  • Time Off: Flexible, unlimited vacation policy

  • Work Hours: Flexible, with the responsiveness and intensity expected from a company-building leadership role

  • Work Setup: In person in San Francisco; this role owns a meaningful part of Legion’s in-person employee experience

  • Impact: Build the team and operating environment behind a company trying to change health care forever

  • Autonomy and Learning: Own People and Talent end-to-end, with direct access to the founders and visibility into every part of the company

  • Growth Opportunities: With exceptional performance and company growth, this role can develop into VP of People and Talent, Head of People, or another executive leadership position.

📝 How to Apply and Hiring Process

  • Apply here: https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/legionhealth/3f5d8943-7668-4546-8373-54b56b951341/application

  • Overview of our hiring process:

  1. Resume + Application Screen

  2. Founder Interview

  3. Live Working Session or Case Study

  4. Onsite Cross-Functional Interviews with Founders

  5. Professional Reference Checks, including former executives, peers, internal customers, and direct reports where applicable

  • Estimated time-to-hire: 2 weeks

  • Start date: ASAP

  • Hiring manager: Yash Patel, CEO

🤝 Equal Employment Opportunity

Legion Health is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees, contractors, and applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or any other protected characteristic under applicable law. We encourage applicants from all backgrounds to apply.

Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, Legion Health will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

Legion Health is committed to providing reasonable accommodations to qualified individuals with disabilities throughout the application and interview process. Applicants who require an accommodation should inform their recruiting contact.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
🧠 About Legion Health

At Legion Health, we believe everyone deserves fast, affordable, and world-class health care, and we’re developing the AI infrastructure to deliver it ourselves at world scale.

Legion is building autonomous medical care (the AI doctor), starting with psychiatry. Our AI-native care-delivery platform currently automates 95% of the administrative work required for us to deliver direct patient care. We also recently became the first company ever to receive regulatory authorization to let AI prescribe psychiatric medications, allowing us to not only collapse health care’s admin costs but also its clinical labor costs—shifting this industry’s economics from humans to tokens.

Our technical moat is hard to copy—we combine rich data, production AI, doctors in the loop, and end-to-end care operations to deliver measurably better care to a clinically complex patient population. This has helped us produce tens of thousands of total visits in just 2 years, all while holding ops costs flat and achieving industry-leading patient NPS and retention. While the last generation of healthcare startups made the existing system incrementally more efficient, Legion is rebuilding full-stack care delivery from first principles. Our vision? A 10X better patient experience that’s higher quality, less expensive, and more scalable than ever before. And a 10X better clinician experience that frees our providers to focus on what matters most: caring for patients.

Legion Health is backed by Y Combinator, leading venture capital firms, and founders from Function Health, Modern Health, Everly Health, Trusted Health, Clipboard Health, PatientPing, Sesame Care, Faire, EasyPost, and fuboTV.

Join us as we build the future of health care: faster, higher-quality, and more affordable, powered by doctors and AI working together.

 

📍 Role Logistics

  • Job Type: Full-Time

  • Role Type: Provider Partnerships / Field Sales / Referral Growth / Growth / Sales

  • Ideal Experience Level: 4+ years carrying and hitting a quota in a full-cycle, customer-facing role

  • Location: Regional territory (field-based), with occasional travel for team offsites and strategic meetings

  • US Visa Sponsorship: No

🚀 The Opportunity

Legion is hiring a Provider Partnership Manager to build and own the referral relationships that connect providers to Legion's psychiatric care. This is a ground-floor, quota-carrying role on a brand-new team: you'll be one of Legion's first dedicated field sales hires, which means you'll help define the playbook, not just run it.

PCPs see mental health needs in their patients every day but rarely have a fast, trusted place to send patients. You'll be that trusted place — building in-person relationships with physicians, medical assistants, office managers, and administrators that turn a single conversation into a durable referral pipeline.

You will own your defined territory like a business: unlocking new practice relationships, running the full partnership cycle, and growing referral volume in accounts you've already won.

✅ Responsibilities and Deliverables

  • Carry a quota for provider referral partnerships and referral volume in your territory, and treat it as your scoreboard.

  • Run the full cycle: self-source through prospecting, build the case with practice decision-makers, and close.

  • Keep your pipeline and account activity clean and current in the CRM.

  • Spend the majority of your week in the field meeting with physicians, medical assistants, office managers, and administrators; supplement with virtual outreach and follow-up.

  • Represent Legion credibly to clinical and administrative customers, translating a new category of AI-enabled psychiatric care into a clear, compelling referral case.

  • Map the decision-making unit inside each practice and build multi-threaded relationships that move a partnership from first meeting to live referrals.

  • Become a trusted resource to providers by educating them on Legion's model and the impact fast, accessible psychiatric care has on their patients.

  • Set each practice up for a clean handoff so patient referrals convert into scheduled visits.

  • Feed what you learn in the field back into messaging, targeting, and the sales playbook. You're building this function, not inheriting it.

  • Partner with leadership on territory design, targeting, and process as the team scales.

  • Collaborate with your peers across territories sharing what's working, troubleshooting objections together, and helping build a team where everyone's win rate goes up.

🏆 You’ll Be Successful If You…

  • Are driven by the number: hitting quota is satisfying, beating it is the point, and you don't need anyone chasing you for it.

  • Would rather write the playbook than inherit one, and see the ambiguity of a new category as opportunity, not friction.

  • Earn trust with physicians quickly. You can get in front of a busy clinician, read the room, and move a skeptical conversation toward a signed partnership.

  • Treat change as normal. Territories, tooling, and the field/virtual mix will evolve as we scale, and you adapt fast while staying focused on results.

  • Are energized by the mission of making fast, affordable psychiatric care accessible through better referral pathways.

  • Welcome coaching and feedback and treat growth as a team sport.

🧰 Ideal Background and Skills

  • 4+ years carrying and hitting a quota in a field-based or B2B2C role; healthcare, medical device, or pharma referral sales strongly preferred.

  • Comfort and skill in front of clinical and administrative buyers; you can build physician rapport and move a conversation toward a partnership.

  • Strength selling in person, with the judgment to know what a given relationship needs.

  • Highly organized and analytical, comfortable owning a number and reasoning from your own pipeline data.

  • Strong written and verbal communication, with the polish to represent Legion well externally.

  • Familiarity with CRM and sales tooling.

  • Existing relationships with provider referral networks are a plus, but not required.

💰 Compensation & Benefits

  • Comp: OTE range of $120,000 to $180,000 depending on experience. Competitive base + uncapped, performance-based variable commission tied to your number, plus meaningful early-stage equity

  • Additional Perks: Mileage and travel reimbursement at the IRS standard rate, coverage for field and provider engagement expenses, cell phone stipend

  • Time Off: Flexible, unlimited vacation policy

  • Work Setup: Remote, in-field with some travel for team meetings

  • Benefits: Comprehensive health, dental, and vision coverage

  • Impact: Build the referral engine that connects primary care to the future of psychiatric care

  • Growth Opportunities: As we scale, this role can grow into a leadership role, building out enablement or larger partnership role.

📝 How to Apply and Hiring Process

  • Apply here: https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/legionhealth/2289fb02-74da-4f4c-8ffc-e5973a39329c/application

  • Overview of our hiring process:

    1. Recruiter Screen

    2. Hiring Manager Interview

    3. Founder Interviews (2)

    4. Professional Reference Checks

  • Estimated time-to-hire: 3 weeks

  • Start date: ASAP

🤝 Equal Employment Opportunity

Legion Health is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees, contractors, and applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or any other protected characteristic under applicable law. We encourage applicants from all backgrounds to apply.

jobs.title: Remote Provider Operations Virtual Assistant — Recruiting, Onboarding, and Payroll (backed by Y Combinator, $5M+ ARR, $23M+ raised)
jobs.descriptionHtml:
🧠 About Legion Health

At Legion Health, we believe everyone deserves fast, affordable, and world-class health care, and we’re developing the AI infrastructure to deliver it at scale.

Legion is building autonomous medical care, starting with psychiatry. Our AI-native care-delivery platform automates much of the administrative work required to deliver direct patient care, allowing clinicians and operations teams to focus on the moments where human judgment and attention matter most.

Our technical moat is hard to copy—we combine rich data, production AI, doctors in the loop, and end-to-end care operations to deliver measurably better care to a clinically complex patient population. This has helped us complete tens of thousands of visits in just two years while holding operations costs flat and achieving industry-leading patient NPS and retention.

While the last generation of healthcare startups made the existing system incrementally more efficient, Legion is rebuilding full-stack care delivery from first principles. Our vision is a 10X better patient experience that is higher quality, less expensive, and more scalable—and a 10X better clinician experience that frees providers to focus on what matters most: caring for patients.

Legion Health is backed by Y Combinator, leading venture capital firms, and founders from Function Health, Modern Health, Everly Health, Trusted Health, Clipboard Health, PatientPing, Sesame Care, Faire, EasyPost, and fuboTV.

Join us as we build the future of health care: faster, higher-quality, and more affordable, powered by clinicians, operators, and AI working together.

📍 Role Logistics

  • Job Type: Full-time contract

  • Role Type: Provider Operations / Recruiting Coordination / Onboarding / Payroll Support

  • Ideal Experience Level: 2+ years

  • Location: Fully remote

  • Work Hours: 9:00 AM–6:00 PM US Central Time

  • Hourly Compensation: $5–$15 per hour, based on experience

🚀 The Opportunity

Legion is hiring an exceptionally organized and detail-oriented Medical Virtual Assistant to help operate the systems that support our growing network of healthcare providers.

You will support providers throughout their relationship with Legion—from recruiting and onboarding through active operations, payroll preparation, and offboarding. Your work will help ensure candidates receive timely follow-up, new providers are ready to begin, operating records remain accurate, and payroll inputs are complete before they are finalized.

This is not a generic assistant role. You will own recurring, detail-heavy workflows that directly affect providers, internal teams, and Legion’s ability to deliver patient care. A missed document can delay a provider’s start date. An inaccurate status field can create confusion across teams. An overlooked payroll discrepancy can affect a provider’s pay. Precision and follow-through matter.

The right person enjoys bringing order to complex workflows. You should be comfortable maintaining spreadsheets and trackers, coordinating across multiple teams, following up persistently, documenting decisions, and identifying missing information before it becomes a larger problem.

This role is a strong fit for someone who enjoys checklists, healthcare operations, provider communication, reconciliation work, and continuously improving how recurring processes are run.

✅ Responsibilities and Deliverables

  • Coordinate provider recruiting operations, including:

    • Maintaining accurate candidate records and statuses.

    • Scheduling and confirming interviews.

    • Following up with candidates about outstanding steps.

    • Updating hiring records and internal trackers.

    • Coordinating handoffs between recruiting and onboarding.

  • Support provider onboarding from accepted offer through start readiness, including:

    • Collecting required documents and information.

    • Maintaining onboarding checklists and status trackers.

    • Following up promptly on missing or incomplete items.

    • Coordinating internal handoffs across relevant teams.

    • Confirming that required operational steps are complete before a provider begins.

    • Escalating blockers that could delay a provider’s start date.

  • Maintain accurate provider-operations records, including:

    • Provider rosters.

    • Recruiting and onboarding status.

    • Active, inactive, and offboarding providers.

    • State coverage and provider availability.

    • Collaborating-physician relationships.

    • Credentialing and payer-enrollment status.

    • Outstanding documents, approvals, and follow-up items.

  • Communicate clearly and professionally with providers through Slack, email, and approved internal systems.

  • Support weekly payroll preparation, including:

    • Gathering provider compensation inputs from approved systems.

    • Reviewing visit counts, no-shows, and late cancellations.

    • Updating payroll and payment trackers.

    • Reconciling discrepancies across source systems.

    • Confirming that supporting information is complete.

    • Escalating unresolved discrepancies before payroll is finalized.

    • Maintaining a clear record of changes, questions, and resolutions.

  • Coordinate across recruiting, credentialing, clinical operations, billing, finance, and payroll to keep provider workflows moving.

  • Maintain clear task queues and follow-up systems so that outstanding items do not fall through the cracks.

  • Document recurring workflows and update SOPs, checklists, and templates as processes evolve.

  • Identify opportunities to simplify, standardize, or automate repetitive administrative work.

  • Handle sensitive provider, company, hiring, and compensation information with discretion and care.

  • Raise unclear ownership, conflicting information, or potential errors promptly rather than making unsupported assumptions.

🏆 You’ll Be Successful If You…

  • Keep provider trackers accurate, current, and easy for other teams to understand.

  • Ensure candidates and providers receive timely, professional follow-up.

  • Help new providers complete onboarding requirements and become ready to start without preventable delays.

  • Catch missing information and payroll discrepancies before they create downstream problems.

  • Produce documentation that clearly explains what happened, what remains outstanding, and who owns the next step.

  • Manage recurring deadlines without needing repeated reminders.

  • Follow established procedures while noticing when a process is unclear, inefficient, or incomplete.

  • Move quickly without sacrificing accuracy.

  • Communicate professionally and confidently with clinicians, candidates, contractors, and internal teammates.

  • Remain calm and organized when priorities change or multiple deadlines overlap.

  • Build reusable checklists, trackers, and workflows that make provider operations easier to scale.

  • Earn the trust of providers and teammates through reliability, discretion, accuracy, and consistent follow-through.

🧰 Ideal Background and Skills

  • 2+ years of experience in one or more of the following:

    • Healthcare operations.

    • Provider operations.

    • Recruiting coordination.

    • Provider or employee onboarding.

    • Payroll or invoice support.

    • Human-resources administration.

    • Executive-assistant or virtual-operations support.

  • Strong preference for experience supporting:

    • Clinicians or other healthcare professionals.

    • Independent contractors.

    • Distributed or fully remote teams.

    • Recurring payroll, payment, or reconciliation workflows.

  • Excellent organizational skills and close attention to detail.

  • Strong spreadsheet skills, including maintaining structured trackers, reviewing data, reconciling differences, and identifying missing information.

  • Careful with names, dates, pay periods, visit counts, status fields, and supporting documentation.

  • Clear, concise, and professional written English.

  • Comfortable following up persistently and respectfully with providers and internal teammates.

  • Able to manage several recurring workflows and deadlines simultaneously.

  • Proactive about identifying blockers, discrepancies, unclear ownership, and overdue action items.

  • Comfortable working in a fast-moving startup where processes may evolve as the company grows.

  • Able to handle confidential provider, recruiting, company, and compensation information appropriately.

  • Familiarity with HIPAA-sensitive healthcare environments and appropriate information-handling practices.

  • Experience with any of the following is a plus:

    • Google Sheets.

    • Slack.

    • Ashby or another applicant-tracking system.

    • Healthie or another EHR or practice-management platform.

    • Looker Studio or similar reporting tools.

    • Stripe or contractor-payment platforms.

    • Payroll, invoicing, or payment-reconciliation workflows.

    • Telehealth or behavioral-health operations.

    • Credentialing and payer enrollment.

    • Healthcare billing.

    • Provider scheduling or workforce operations.

⚠️ This Role Is Not a Fit If You…

  • Prefer exclusively patient-facing work and do not enjoy internal operations.

  • Dislike spreadsheets, trackers, checklists, or reconciliation work.

  • Need every day to follow exactly the same workflow.

  • Wait for repeated instructions instead of proactively following up on outstanding work.

  • Are uncomfortable asking questions or escalating conflicting information.

  • Are casual about deadlines, documentation, confidentiality, or payroll accuracy.

  • Frequently lose track of details when managing several workflows at once.

  • Prefer completing individual tasks without taking ownership of the full outcome.

💰 Compensation & Role Benefits

  • Hourly Compensation: $5–$15 per hour, based on experience.

  • Job Type: Full-time contract.

  • Schedule: 9:00 AM–6:00 PM US Central Time.

  • Work Setup: Fully remote.

  • Impact: Build the provider-operations foundation that enables clinicians to spend more time caring for patients.

  • Autonomy and Learning: Develop experience across recruiting coordination, provider onboarding, healthcare operations, payroll preparation, and process improvement.

  • Growth Opportunities: Take on broader ownership across provider operations, onboarding, recruiting coordination, payroll operations, quality assurance, or team leadership as Legion grows.

🤝 Equal Employment Opportunity

Legion Health is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees, contractors, and applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or any other protected characteristic under applicable law. We encourage applicants from all backgrounds to apply.

   - Reviewing visit counts, no-shows, and late cancellations.
   
   - Updating payroll and payment trackers.
   
   - Reconciling discrepancies across source systems.
   
   - Confirming that supporting information is complete.
   
   - Escalating unresolved discrepancies before payroll is finalized.
   
   - Maintaining a clear record of changes, questions, and resolutions.

 - Coordinate across recruiting, credentialing, clinical operations, billing, finance, and payroll to keep provider workflows moving.

 - Maintain clear task queues and follow-up systems so that outstanding items do not fall through the cracks.

 - Document recurring workflows and update SOPs, checklists, and templates as processes evolve.

 - Identify opportunities to simplify, standardize, or automate repetitive administrative work.

 - Handle sensitive provider, company, hiring, and compensation information with discretion and care.

 - Raise unclear ownership, conflicting information, or potential errors promptly rather than making unsupported assumptions.




🏆 YOU’LL BE SUCCESSFUL IF YOU…

 - Keep provider trackers accurate, current, and easy for other teams to understand.

 - Ensure candidates and providers receive timely, professional follow-up.

 - Help new providers complete onboarding requirements and become ready to start without preventable delays.

 - Catch missing information and payroll discrepancies before they create downstream problems.

 - Produce documentation that clearly explains what happened, what remains outstanding, and who owns the next step.

 - Manage recurring deadlines without needing repeated reminders.

 - Follow established procedures while noticing when a process is unclear, inefficient, or incomplete.

 - Move quickly without sacrificing accuracy.

 - Communicate professionally and confidently with clinicians, candidates, contractors, and internal teammates.

 - Remain calm and organized when priorities change or multiple deadlines overlap.

 - Build reusable checklists, trackers, and workflows that make provider operations easier to scale.

 - Earn the trust of providers and teammates through reliability, discretion, accuracy, and consistent follow-through.




🧰 IDEAL BACKGROUND AND SKILLS

 - 2+ years of experience in one or more of the following:
   
   - Healthcare operations.
   
   - Provider operations.
   
   - Recruiting coordination.
   
   - Provider or employee onboarding.
   
   - Payroll or invoice support.
   
   - Human-resources administration.
   
   - Executive-assistant or virtual-operations support.

 - Strong preference for experience supporting:
   
   - Clinicians or other healthcare professionals.
   
   - Independent contractors.
   
   - Distributed or fully remote teams.
   
   - Recurring payroll, payment, or reconciliation workflows.

 - Excellent organizational skills and close attention to detail.

 - Strong spreadsheet skills, including maintaining structured trackers, reviewing data, reconciling differences, and identifying missing information.

 - Careful with names, dates, pay periods, visit counts, status fields, and supporting documentation.

 - Clear, concise, and professional written English.

 - Comfortable following up persistently and respectfully with providers and internal teammates.

 - Able to manage several recurring workflows and deadlines simultaneously.

 - Proactive about identifying blockers, discrepancies, unclear ownership, and overdue action items.

 - Comfortable working in a fast-moving startup where processes may evolve as the company grows.

 - Able to handle confidential provider, recruiting, company, and compensation information appropriately.

 - Familiarity with HIPAA-sensitive healthcare environments and appropriate information-handling practices.

 - Experience with any of the following is a plus:
   
   - Google Sheets.
   
   - Slack.
   
   - Ashby or another applicant-tracking system.
   
   - Healthie or another EHR or practice-management platform.
   
   - Looker Studio or similar reporting tools.
   
   - Stripe or contractor-payment platforms.
   
   - Payroll, invoicing, or payment-reconciliation workflows.
   
   - Telehealth or behavioral-health operations.
   
   - Credentialing and payer enrollment.
   
   - Healthcare billing.
   
   - Provider scheduling or workforce operations.




⚠️ THIS ROLE IS NOT A FIT IF YOU…

 - Prefer exclusively patient-facing work and do not enjoy internal operations.

 - Dislike spreadsheets, trackers, checklists, or reconciliation work.

 - Need every day to follow exactly the same workflow.

 - Wait for repeated instructions instead of proactively following up on outstanding work.

 - Are uncomfortable asking questions or escalating conflicting information.

 - Are casual about deadlines, documentation, confidentiality, or payroll accuracy.

 - Frequently lose track of details when managing several workflows at once.

 - Prefer completing individual tasks without taking ownership of the full outcome.




💰 COMPENSATION & ROLE BENEFITS

 - Hourly Compensation: $5–$15 per hour, based on experience.

 - Job Type: Full-time contract.

 - Schedule: 9:00 AM–6:00 PM US Central Time.

 - Work Setup: Fully remote.

 - Impact: Build the provider-operations foundation that enables clinicians to spend more time caring for patients.

 - Autonomy and Learning: Develop experience across recruiting coordination, provider onboarding, healthcare operations, payroll preparation, and process improvement.

 - Growth Opportunities: Take on broader ownership across provider operations, onboarding, recruiting coordination, payroll operations, quality assurance, or team leadership as Legion grows.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
🧠 About Legion Health

At Legion Health, we believe everyone deserves fast, affordable, and world-class health care, and we’re developing the AI infrastructure to deliver it at scale.

Legion is building autonomous medical care, starting with psychiatry. Our AI-native care-delivery platform automates much of the administrative work required to deliver direct patient care, allowing clinicians and patient-support teams to focus on the moments where human judgment and empathy matter most.

Our technical moat is hard to copy—we combine rich data, production AI, doctors in the loop, and end-to-end care operations to deliver measurably better care to a clinically complex patient population. This has helped us complete tens of thousands of visits in just two years while holding operations costs flat and achieving industry-leading patient NPS and retention.

While the last generation of healthcare startups made the existing system incrementally more efficient, Legion is rebuilding full-stack care delivery from first principles. Our vision is a 10X better patient experience that is higher quality, less expensive, and more scalable—and a 10X better clinician experience that frees providers to focus on what matters most: caring for patients.

Legion Health is backed by Y Combinator, leading venture capital firms, and founders from Function Health, Modern Health, Everly Health, Trusted Health, Clipboard Health, PatientPing, Sesame Care, Faire, EasyPost, and fuboTV.

Join us as we build the future of health care: faster, higher-quality, and more affordable, powered by clinicians, patient-support professionals, and AI working together.

📍 Role Logistics

  • Job Type: Contract

  • Role Type: Patient Experience / Patient Success / Care Coordination

  • Ideal Experience Level: 2+ years

  • Location: Fully remote

  • Work Hours: 8-hour shift between 6:00 AM and 10:00 PM Central Time

  • Hourly Compensation: $5–$15 per hour, based on experience

🚀 The Opportunity

Legion is hiring a compassionate, highly organized Patient Experience Representative to support patients throughout their care journey.

You will communicate directly with patients by phone and messaging, help them navigate operational barriers, coordinate administrative and clinical-support workflows, and ensure that every interaction has a clear next step. Your work will help patients feel heard, informed, and supported while making it easier for Legion’s clinicians to deliver timely care.

This is not a traditional customer-service role. You will support real patients who may be anxious, frustrated, confused, or experiencing delays in their care. You must be able to communicate calmly and empathetically while gathering accurate information, setting appropriate expectations, documenting each interaction, and following through until the issue is resolved or transferred to the correct team.

You will also help patients remain engaged in care through proactive follow-ups, appointment reminders, and outreach. Strong patient support is not only about responding to questions—it is about anticipating barriers, preventing patients from falling through the cracks, and making a complicated healthcare experience feel clear and manageable.

This is a fast-moving startup environment. The right person is adaptable, dependable, comfortable managing multiple patient conversations, and proactive about improving the workflows behind the patient experience.

This is a strictly non-clinical role. You will not provide medical advice, diagnose patients, interpret symptoms, recommend treatment, or make clinical decisions. You will work closely with clinical teams by gathering information, supporting logistics, documenting requests, and routing clinical matters to the appropriate licensed professional.

✅ Responsibilities and Deliverables

  • Respond to patient questions across phone and messaging platforms with clear, accurate, timely, and compassionate communication.

  • Help patients understand what to expect and what actions they need to take next.

  • Support appointment scheduling, rescheduling, cancellations, and patient onboarding.

  • Conduct proactive outreach, reminders, and follow-ups to help patients remain engaged in care.

  • Follow up with patients who have missed appointments, incomplete tasks, unresolved questions, or other barriers to continuing care.

  • Support patient-retention workflows by identifying problems early and helping patients reach the correct team or next step.

  • Coordinate administrative and clinical-support workflows, including:

    • Prior authorizations: Gather required information, track status, follow up on outstanding steps, and escalate delays.

    • Prescription and refill requests: Collect the patient’s request, document it accurately, and route it to the appropriate clinical team.

    • FMLA and documentation requests: Complete intake, gather required information, route the request, track progress, and follow up.

    • Pharmacy coordination: Help resolve logistical questions and route medication-related decisions to licensed clinical staff.

    • Insurance and billing questions: Gather context and coordinate with the appropriate internal team.

    • General patient administration: Manage follow-ups, forms, records requests, and cross-functional coordination.

  • Document every material patient interaction accurately so teammates and clinicians understand what happened, what remains outstanding, and who owns the next step.

  • Maintain clear follow-up queues and ensure unresolved patient needs do not fall through the cracks.

  • Recognize urgent, sensitive, clinical, or safety-related concerns and follow the appropriate escalation procedure immediately.

  • Coordinate with clinical operations, providers, billing, pharmacy-support, and other internal teams to resolve patient concerns.

  • Communicate realistic expectations without making promises outside your authority.

  • Follow approved scripts, SOPs, privacy requirements, and escalation protocols.

  • Identify recurring patient questions, delays, and sources of confusion and share actionable feedback with the appropriate teams.

  • Help improve patient-support templates, scripts, checklists, and standard operating procedures.

  • Use approved systems consistently and maintain a reliable, high-speed internet connection and professional environment for patient calls.

  • Protect patient privacy and handle sensitive information according to Legion’s policies and approved systems.

  • Consistently aim to deliver the best possible experience for every patient and family.

🏆 You’ll Be Successful If You…

  • Make patients feel heard, respected, and supported—even when they are frustrated, worried, or confused.

  • Communicate clearly and professionally in both spoken and written English.

  • Explain next steps simply without sounding robotic, rushed, dismissive, or overly technical.

  • Respond promptly and follow through consistently until each issue is resolved or transferred to the correct owner.

  • Help patients remain engaged in care by reducing preventable confusion, delays, and administrative barriers.

  • Manage multiple patient conversations and follow-up tasks without losing important details.

  • Produce concise, accurate documentation that enables other teammates to act without repeating the entire conversation.

  • Distinguish between administrative support and clinical decision-making.

  • Recognize when an issue is outside your scope and escalate it promptly through the correct channel.

  • Stay calm and use sound judgment during sensitive or emotionally difficult conversations.

  • Learn Legion’s care model, patient workflows, systems, scripts, and escalation paths quickly.

  • Follow established processes while identifying opportunities to make patient support faster, clearer, and more reliable.

  • Adapt constructively as workflows change in a growing startup.

  • Earn the trust of patients, clinicians, and teammates through empathy, reliability, discretion, and excellent follow-through.

🧰 Ideal Background and Skills

  • 2+ years of experience in a patient-facing support or healthcare-operations role.

  • Experience in one or more of the following is strongly preferred:

    • Behavioral health or psychiatry.

    • Digital health or telehealth.

    • Healthcare call centers.

    • Patient access or patient experience.

    • Nursing or medical administration.

    • Pharmacy support.

    • Insurance or prior-authorization support.

    • Care coordination.

  • Exceptional spoken and written English.

  • Warm, clear, confident, and professional communication on patient phone calls.

  • Strong patient empathy and the ability to remain calm during sensitive conversations.

  • Excellent organization, attention to detail, and follow-through.

  • Experience managing a high volume of calls, messages, cases, or patient-support requests.

  • Familiarity with healthcare workflows such as scheduling, insurance, pharmacies, prior authorizations, refills, medical documentation, and patient forms.

  • Experience working in a telehealth or healthcare call-center environment is highly preferred.

  • Comfort using tools such as Dialpad, Slack, Healthie, EHRs, CRMs, ticketing systems, or similar platforms.

  • Ability to work closely with clinical teams while remaining firmly within a non-clinical scope.

  • Comfort working in a fast-paced startup where workflows and priorities may evolve.

  • A clinical or healthcare background—such as medical-assistant, CNA, nursing, behavioral-health, or pharmacy experience—is helpful but not required.

  • A reliable computer, high-speed internet connection, and quiet, professional environment for patient calls.

The most important qualifications are patient empathy, excellent communication, operational execution, sound judgment, accurate documentation, and reliable follow-through.

⚕️ Non-Clinical Scope

This is a non-clinical patient-support role.

  • You will not diagnose patients or assess medical conditions.

  • You will not provide medical or medication advice.

  • You will not recommend or make treatment decisions.

  • You will not interpret symptoms, laboratory results, or clinical records for patients.

  • You will not approve prescriptions, refills, prior authorizations, or medical documentation.

  • You will route clinical, medication, safety, and treatment questions to the appropriate licensed team member.

Your responsibility is to support patient communication, logistics, documentation, coordination, and escalation so patients can receive timely care from the appropriate clinical team.

⚠️ This Role Is Not a Fit If You…

  • Are uncomfortable speaking with patients regularly by phone.

  • Prefer work that does not involve emotionally sensitive or occasionally difficult conversations.

  • Struggle to communicate clearly and professionally in spoken or written English.

  • Dislike detailed documentation, follow-up queues, or repetitive coordination work.

  • Frequently lose track of details when managing several conversations or cases.

  • Wait for repeated instructions instead of proactively following up on unresolved issues.

  • Are uncomfortable adapting when processes change.

  • Want to provide clinical advice or make treatment decisions in this role.

  • Are casual about privacy, documentation, attendance, response times, or follow-through.

💰 Compensation & Role Benefits

  • Hourly Compensation: $5–$15 per hour, based on experience.

  • Job Type: Contract.

  • Schedule: 8-hour shift between 6:00 AM and 10:00 PM Central Time

  • Work Setup: Fully remote.

  • Impact: Help patients and families navigate mental-health care with greater clarity, continuity, and support.

  • Autonomy and Learning: Develop experience across patient experience, telehealth operations, care coordination, healthcare administration, and behavioral-health workflows.

  • Growth Opportunities: Take on broader ownership across patient experience, quality assurance, training, workflow improvement, or team leadership as Legion grows.

🤝 Equal Employment Opportunity

Legion Health is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees, contractors, and applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or any other protected characteristic under applicable law. We encourage applicants from all backgrounds to apply.

jobs.title: Staff Psychiatrist (MD or DO) — Remote | Telehealth | Full-Time or Part-Time | Multiple States
jobs.descriptionHtml:
[We show compassion to heal minds.]

 

🧠 About Legion Health

Legion Health is a technology-forward psychiatry company delivering world-class outpatient mental health care while expanding access for patients through insurance.

We are seeking exceptional Psychiatrists (MD or DO) across the United States who are passionate about evidence-based psychiatry and want the time, support, and clinical autonomy needed to provide exceptional patient care.

Our innovative model combines the stability of a traditional hospital position with the flexibility of a private practice. We prioritize our clinicians' well-being and professional growth, offering a competitive compensation package and fostering a vibrant, collaborative culture.

Quality and patient experience are paramount to us. This means recruiting exceptional providers, championing evidence-based protocols, and displaying compassion in every patient interaction. Our exceptional psychiatrists operate with clinical autonomy, supported by experienced peers.

Our vision is to pioneer a new era of medicine by delivering world-class psychiatry. We believe in a future where every person can access the compassionate, high-quality care they need.

 

🚀 About the Role

Practice at the top of your license, from wherever you do your best work. This role is designed for psychiatrists who want meaningful clinical autonomy without having to build and operate a private practice alone.

We are looking for clinically excellent, patient-centered psychiatrists to provide psychiatric care through telehealth. Full-time and part-time positions are available.

 

💙 Benefits

Legion’s model is built to give clinicians more time for patients, fewer administrative distractions, and the support of a high-caliber psychiatric community.

  • Flexibility: Set your own schedule for optimal work-life balance.

  • Work from Home: See patients from the comfort of your home via telehealth.

  • Significant Administrative Support: You focus on patient care, and we’ll handle scheduling, insurance verification, billing, prior authorizations, pharmacy coordination, etc.

  • Patient Acquisition: Unlike with a private practice, we’ll work to fill your schedule, so you don’t have to do your own marketing.

  • Competitive Pay: We compensate our providers at market-leading rates.

  • Weekly Pay: We pay our providers every week for immediate financial benefit and planning ease.

  • Legal Protection: We provide full malpractice insurance coverage.

  • Clinical Autonomy: We hire the most skilled providers and trust them to do what’s best for patients.

  • Technical Support: We cover the costs for you to have best-in-class EHR, e-Prescribe, and AI tools.

  • Credentialing Support: We handle all aspects and costs of credentialing with a large number of insurance plans, including commercial, ACA, and government, ensuring your legal and effective authorization within insurance networks.

  • Licensure and DEA Coverage: We’ll reimburse you for all fees associated with getting licensed in other states as required by Legion.

  • Commitment to Responsible Prescribing and High-Quality Care: We have rigorous, evidence-based protocols and provide objective diagnostic tools to ensure responsible and ethical prescriptions of controlled substances.

  • Community of Clinical Excellence: You will work alongside the most talented psychiatrists in the world. Our current psychiatrists have trained at some of the country’s most prestigious institutions.

  • Opportunities for Professional Growth: As we expand, we intend to promote clinical leadership from the best of our active providers.

  • Culture of Excellence through Innovation: Actively participate in ushering in a new era of mental health care through superior clinical care and technology.

  • Resources: We provide premium subscriptions to resources such as UpToDate and Carlat.

  • Exclusive Events: Engage with your colleagues through exclusive in-person and virtual events.

 

✅ Responsibilities

  • Provide excellent patient care for conditions including depression, anxiety, ADHD, insomnia, PTSD, bipolar disorder, etc.

  • Perform comprehensive psychiatric assessments, including mental-health history, medical history, diagnostic evaluation, and risk analysis.

  • Create and execute individualized treatment plans that may combine medication management and brief psychotherapy.

  • Provide compassionate, respectful, and patient-centered care.

  • Use evidence-based clinical protocols and responsible prescribing practices.

  • Collaborate with other psychiatrists through consultations and case reviews.

  • Use technology and operational systems effectively to deliver reliable telehealth care.

 

🧰 Qualifications

  • An active, unrestricted license to practice medicine in at least one U.S. jurisdiction.

  • Strong clinical assessment, diagnostic, and medication-management skills.

  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.

  • Comfort providing care remotely and using electronic health record systems.

  • Commitment to patient-centered, compassionate, evidence-based care.

 

📍 Role Logistics

  • Location: Fully remote within the United States.

  • Schedule: Full-time or part-time positions are available.

  • Expected annual compensation: $300K–$500K, depending on completed patient-care hours.

 

🤝 Clinical Advisory Board

Legion’s Clinical Advisory Board brings together nationally recognized psychiatrists, physician executives, telepsychiatry pioneers, and primary-care leaders. Working closely with Legion’s medical leadership, they help shape our clinical quality standards, evidence-based care protocols, prescribing safeguards, risk-management practices, and continuous quality-improvement efforts as the company scales.

Members of our clinical advisory board include:

  • Madhukar Trivedi, M.D. — Psychiatrist; Professor of Psychiatry and Distinguished Chair in Mental Health at UT Southwestern

  • Collaborating Physician Coverage: Where applicable, we provide your collaborating psychiatrist and fully cover the costs.
