  • Weekly Pay: We pay our providers every week for immediate financial benefit and planning ease.

  • Legal Protection: We provide full malpractice insurance coverage.

  • Clinical Autonomy: We hire the most skilled providers and trust them to do what’s best for patients.

  • Technical Support: We cover the costs for you to have best-in-class EHR, e-Prescribe, and AI tools.

  • Credentialing Support: We handle all aspects and costs of credentialing with a large number of insurance plans, including commercial, ACA, and government, ensuring your legal and effective authorization within insurance networks.

  • Licensure and DEA Coverage: We’ll reimburse you for all fees associated with getting licensed in other states as required by Legion.

  • Commitment to Responsible Prescribing and High-Quality Care: We have rigorous, evidence-based protocols and provide objective diagnostic tools to ensure responsible and ethical prescriptions of controlled substances.

  • Collaborate with psychiatrists and clinical peers through consultations and case reviews.

  • Use technology and operational systems effectively to deliver reliable telehealth care.

  • Comfort providing care remotely and using electronic health record systems.

  • Commitment to patient-centered, compassionate, evidence-based care.

 

📍 Role Logistics

  • Jon Kole, M.D. — Psychiatrist; Senior Medical Director at Headspace

  • Liberty Eberly, D.O. — Psychiatrist; Co-Founder and Former Chief Medical Officer at innovaTel Telepsychiatry

  • John Lusins, M.D. — Psychiatrist; Founder and President at South Texas Mental Health Associates

  • Jacqueline Champlain, M.D. — Family Medicine Physician; Lead Physician at WellMed and Fellow of the American Academy of Family Physicians

We encourage applicants from all backgrounds to apply.

🧠 ABOUT LEGION HEALTH

Legion Health is a technology-forward psychiatry company delivering world-class outpatient mental health care while expanding access for patients through insurance.

We are seeking exceptional Psychiatric Mental Health Nurse Practitioners (PMHNPs) across the United States who are passionate about evidence-based psychiatry and want the time, support, and clinical autonomy needed to provide exceptional patient care.

Our innovative model combines the stability of a traditional hospital position with the flexibility of a private practice. We prioritize our clinicians' well-being and professional growth, offering a competitive compensation package and fostering a vibrant, collaborative culture.

Quality and patient experience are paramount to us. This means recruiting exceptional providers, championing evidence-based protocols, and displaying compassion in every patient interaction. Our exceptional PMHNPs operate with clinical autonomy, supported by experienced psychiatrists through consults and peer case reviews.

Our vision is to pioneer a new era of medicine by delivering world-class psychiatry. We believe in a future where every person can access the compassionate, high-quality care they need.

 


🚀 ABOUT THE ROLE

Practice at the top of your license, from wherever you do your best work. This role is designed for PMHNPs who want meaningful clinical autonomy without having to build and operate a private practice alone.

We are looking for clinically excellent, patient-centered PMHNPs to provide psychiatric care through telehealth. Full-time and part-time positions are available.

 


💙 BENEFITS

Legion’s model is built to give clinicians more time for patients, fewer administrative distractions, and the support of a high-caliber psychiatric community.

 - Flexibility: Set your own schedule for optimal work-life balance.

 - Work from Home: See patients from the comfort of your home via telehealth.

 - Significant Administrative Support: You focus on patient care, and we’ll handle scheduling, insurance verification, billing, prior authorizations, pharmacy coordination, etc.

 - Patient Acquisition: Unlike with a private practice, we’ll work to fill your schedule, so you don’t have to do your own marketing.

 - Collaborating Physician Coverage: Where applicable, we provide your collaborating psychiatrist and fully cover the costs.

 - Competitive Pay: We compensate our providers at market-leading rates.

 - Weekly Pay: We pay our providers every week for immediate financial benefit and planning ease.

 - Legal Protection: We provide full malpractice insurance coverage.

 - Clinical Autonomy: We hire the most skilled providers and trust them to do what’s best for patients.

 - Technical Support: We cover the costs for you to have best-in-class EHR, e-Prescribe, and AI tools.

 - Credentialing Support: We handle all aspects and costs of credentialing with a large number of insurance plans, including commercial, ACA, and government, ensuring your legal and effective authorization within insurance networks.

 - Licensure and DEA Coverage: We’ll reimburse you for all fees associated with getting licensed in other states as required by Legion.

 - Commitment to Responsible Prescribing and High-Quality Care: We have rigorous, evidence-based protocols and provide objective diagnostic tools to ensure responsible and ethical prescriptions of controlled substances.

 - Community of Clinical Excellence: You will work alongside the most talented PMHNPs and psychiatrists in the world. Our current PMHNPs have trained at some of the country’s most prestigious institutions, including Vanderbilt, UT Austin, Johns Hopkins, Columbia, NYU, and UTHealth Houston.

 - Opportunities for Professional Growth: As we expand, we intend to promote clinical leadership from the best of our active providers.

 - Culture of Excellence through Innovation: Actively participate in ushering in a new era of mental health care through superior clinical care and technology.

 - Resources: We provide premium subscriptions to resources such as UpToDate and Carlat.

 - Exclusive Events: Engage with your colleagues through exclusive in-person and virtual events.

 


✅ RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Provide excellent patient care for conditions including depression, anxiety, ADHD, insomnia, PTSD, bipolar disorder, etc.

 - Perform comprehensive psychiatric assessments, including mental-health history, medical history, diagnostic evaluation, and risk analysis.

 - Create and execute individualized treatment plans that may combine medication management and brief psychotherapy.

 - Provide compassionate, respectful, and patient-centered care.

 - Use evidence-based clinical protocols and responsible prescribing practices.

 - Collaborate with psychiatrists and clinical peers through consultations and case reviews.

 - Use technology and operational systems effectively to deliver reliable telehealth care.

 


🧰 QUALIFICATIONS

 - Active, unrestricted state-issued authority to practice as a PMHNP in at least one U.S. state or jurisdiction.

 - Strong clinical assessment, diagnostic, and medication-management skills.

 - Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.

 - Comfort providing care remotely and using electronic health record systems.

 - Commitment to patient-centered, compassionate, evidence-based care.

 


📍 ROLE LOGISTICS

 - Location: Fully remote within the United States.

 - Schedule: Full-time or part-time positions are available.

 - Compensation: $150K–$300K per year, depending on completed patient-care hours.

 


🤝 CLINICAL ADVISORY BOARD

Legion’s Clinical Advisory Board brings together nationally recognized psychiatrists, physician executives, telepsychiatry pioneers, and primary-care leaders. Working closely with Legion’s medical leadership, they help shape our clinical quality standards, evidence-based care protocols, prescribing safeguards, risk-management practices, and continuous quality-improvement efforts as the company scales.

Members of our Clinical Advisory Board include:

 - Madhukar Trivedi, M.D. — Psychiatrist; Professor of Psychiatry and Distinguished Chair in Mental Health at UT Southwestern

 - Alexander Ruvalcaba, M.D. — Psychiatrist; Physician Executive at MultiCare Behavioral Health Network

 - Jon Kole, M.D. — Psychiatrist; Senior Medical Director at Headspace

 - Liberty Eberly, D.O. — Psychiatrist; Co-Founder and Former Chief Medical Officer at innovaTel Telepsychiatry

 - John Lusins, M.D. — Psychiatrist; Founder and President at South Texas Mental Health Associates

 - Jacqueline Champlain, M.D. — Family Medicine Physician; Lead Physician at WellMed and Fellow of the American Academy of Family Physicians

 


✨ BRING YOUR BEST CLINICAL WORK TO LEGION

If you are a thoughtful, evidence-based PMHNP who wants the flexibility of remote practice, meaningful clinical autonomy, robust operational support, and a community committed to excellent psychiatric care, we would be excited to learn more about you.

 


🤝 EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY

Legion Health is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees, contractors, and applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or any other protected characteristic under applicable law. We encourage applicants from all backgrounds to apply.

Our exceptional PMHNPs operate with clinical autonomy, supported by experienced psychiatrists through consults and peer case reviews.

Our vision is to pioneer a new era of medicine by delivering world-class psychiatry. We believe in a future where every person can access the compassionate, high-quality care they need.

 


🚀 ABOUT THE ROLE

Practice at the top of your license, from wherever you do your best work. This role is designed for PMHNPs who want meaningful clinical autonomy without having to build and operate a private practice alone.

We are looking for clinically excellent, patient-centered PMHNPs to provide psychiatric care through telehealth. Full-time and part-time positions are available.

 


💙 BENEFITS

Legion’s model is built to give clinicians more time for patients, fewer administrative distractions, and the support of a high-caliber psychiatric community.

 - Flexibility: Set your own schedule for optimal work-life balance.

 - Work from Home: See patients from the comfort of your home via telehealth.

 - Significant Administrative Support: You focus on patient care, and we’ll handle scheduling, insurance verification, billing, prior authorizations, pharmacy coordination, etc.

 - Patient Acquisition: Unlike with a private practice, we’ll work to fill your schedule, so you don’t have to do your own marketing.

 - Collaborating Physician Coverage: Where applicable, we provide your collaborating psychiatrist and fully cover the costs.

 - Competitive Pay: We compensate our providers at market-leading rates.

 - Weekly Pay: We pay our providers every week for immediate financial benefit and planning ease.

 - Legal Protection: We provide full malpractice insurance coverage.

 - Clinical Autonomy: We hire the most skilled providers and trust them to do what’s best for patients.

 - Technical Support: We cover the costs for you to have best-in-class EHR, e-Prescribe, and AI tools.

 - Credentialing Support: We handle all aspects and costs of credentialing with a large number of insurance plans, including commercial, ACA, and government, ensuring your legal and effective authorization within insurance networks.

 - Licensure and DEA Coverage: We’ll reimburse you for all fees associated with getting licensed in other states as required by Legion.

 - Commitment to Responsible Prescribing and High-Quality Care: We have rigorous, evidence-based protocols and provide objective diagnostic tools to ensure responsible and ethical prescriptions of controlled substances.

 - Community of Clinical Excellence: You will work alongside the most talented PMHNPs and psychiatrists in the world. Our current PMHNPs have trained at some of the country’s most prestigious institutions, including Vanderbilt, UT Austin, Johns Hopkins, Columbia, NYU, and UTHealth Houston.

 - Culture of Excellence through Innovation: Actively participate in ushering in a new era of mental health care through superior clinical care and technology.

 - Perform comprehensive psychiatric assessments, including mental-health history, medical history, diagnostic evaluation, and risk analysis.

 - Create and execute individualized treatment plans that may combine medication management and brief psychotherapy.

 - Provide compassionate, respectful, and patient-centered care.

 - Use evidence-based clinical protocols and responsible prescribing practices.

 - Collaborate with psychiatrists and clinical peers through consultations and case reviews.

 - Use technology and operational systems effectively to deliver reliable telehealth care.

 - Active, unrestricted state-issued authority to practice as a PMHNP in at least one U.S. state or jurisdiction.

 - Strong clinical assessment, diagnostic, and medication-management skills.

 - Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.

 - Comfort providing care remotely and using electronic health record systems.

 - Commitment to patient-centered, compassionate, evidence-based care.

 


📍 ROLE LOGISTICS

 - Location: Fully remote within the United States.

 - Schedule: Full-time or part-time positions are available.

 - Compensation: $150K–$300K per year, depending on completed patient-care hours.

 


🤝 CLINICAL ADVISORY BOARD

 - Madhukar Trivedi, M.D. — Psychiatrist; Professor of Psychiatry and Distinguished Chair in Mental Health at UT Southwestern

 - Alexander Ruvalcaba, M.D. — Psychiatrist; Physician Executive at MultiCare Behavioral Health Network

 - Jon Kole, M.D. — Psychiatrist; Senior Medical Director at Headspace

 - Liberty Eberly, D.O. — Psychiatrist; Co-Founder and Former Chief Medical Officer at innovaTel Telepsychiatry

 - John Lusins, M.D. — Psychiatrist; Founder and President at South Texas Mental Health Associates

 - Jacqueline Champlain, M.D. — Family Medicine Physician; Lead Physician at WellMed and Fellow of the American Academy of Family Physicians

 


✨ BRING YOUR BEST CLINICAL WORK TO LEGION

If you are a thoughtful, evidence-based PMHNP who wants the flexibility of remote practice, meaningful clinical autonomy, robust operational support, and a community committed to excellent psychiatric care, we would be excited to learn more about you.

 


🤝 EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY

Legion Health is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees, contractors, and applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or any other protected characteristic under applicable law. We encourage applicants from all backgrounds to apply.

We are looking for clinically excellent, patient-centered PMHNPs to provide psychiatric care through telehealth. Full-time and part-time positions are available.

 


💙 BENEFITS

Legion’s model is built to give clinicians more time for patients, fewer administrative distractions, and the support of a high-caliber psychiatric community.

 - Flexibility: Set your own schedule for optimal work-life balance.

 - Work from Home: See patients from the comfort of your home via telehealth.

 - Significant Administrative Support: You focus on patient care, and we’ll handle scheduling, insurance verification, billing, prior authorizations, pharmacy coordination, etc.

 - Patient Acquisition: Unlike with a private practice, we’ll work to fill your schedule, so you don’t have to do your own marketing.

 - Collaborating Physician Coverage: Where applicable, we provide your collaborating psychiatrist and fully cover the costs.

 - Competitive Pay: We compensate our providers at market-leading rates.

 - Weekly Pay: We pay our providers every week for immediate financial benefit and planning ease.

 - Legal Protection: We provide full malpractice insurance coverage.

 - Clinical Autonomy: We hire the most skilled providers and trust them to do what’s best for patients.

 - Technical Support: We cover the costs for you to have best-in-class EHR, e-Prescribe, and AI tools.

 - Credentialing Support: We handle all aspects and costs of credentialing with a large number of insurance plans, including commercial, ACA, and government, ensuring your legal and effective authorization within insurance networks.

 - Licensure and DEA Coverage: We’ll reimburse you for all fees associated with getting licensed in other states as required by Legion.

 - Commitment to Responsible Prescribing and High-Quality Care: We have rigorous, evidence-based protocols and provide objective diagnostic tools to ensure responsible and ethical prescriptions of controlled substances.

 - Community of Clinical Excellence: You will work alongside the most talented PMHNPs and psychiatrists in the world. Our current PMHNPs have trained at some of the country’s most prestigious institutions, including Vanderbilt, UT Austin, Johns Hopkins, Columbia, NYU, and UTHealth Houston.

 - Culture of Excellence through Innovation: Actively participate in ushering in a new era of mental health care through superior clinical care and technology.

 - Resources: We provide premium subscriptions to resources such as UpToDate and Carlat.

 - Exclusive Events: Engage with your colleagues through exclusive in-person and virtual events.

 - Perform comprehensive psychiatric assessments, including mental-health history, medical history, diagnostic evaluation, and risk analysis.

 - Create and execute individualized treatment plans that may combine medication management and brief psychotherapy.

 - Provide compassionate, respectful, and patient-centered care.

 - Use evidence-based clinical protocols and responsible prescribing practices.

 - Collaborate with psychiatrists and clinical peers through consultations and case reviews.

 - Use technology and operational systems effectively to deliver reliable telehealth care.

 


🧰 QUALIFICATIONS

 - Active, unrestricted state-issued authority to practice as a PMHNP in at least one U.S. state or jurisdiction.

 - Strong clinical assessment, diagnostic, and medication-management skills.

 - Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.

 - Comfort providing care remotely and using electronic health record systems.

 - Commitment to patient-centered, compassionate, evidence-based care.

 


📍 ROLE LOGISTICS

 - Location: Fully remote within the United States.

 - Schedule: Full-time or part-time positions are available.

 - Compensation: $150K–$300K per year, depending on completed patient-care hours.

 


🤝 CLINICAL ADVISORY BOARD

Legion’s Clinical Advisory Board brings together nationally recognized psychiatrists, physician executives, telepsychiatry pioneers, and primary-care leaders.  - Madhukar Trivedi, M.D. — Psychiatrist; Professor of Psychiatry and Distinguished Chair in Mental Health at UT Southwestern

 - Alexander Ruvalcaba, M.D. — Psychiatrist; Physician Executive at MultiCare Behavioral Health Network

 - Jon Kole, M.D. — Psychiatrist; Senior Medical Director at Headspace

 - Liberty Eberly, D.O. — Psychiatrist; Co-Founder and Former Chief Medical Officer at innovaTel Telepsychiatry

 - John Lusins, M.D. — Psychiatrist; Founder and President at South Texas Mental Health Associates

 - Jacqueline Champlain, M.D. — Family Medicine Physician; Lead Physician at WellMed and Fellow of the American Academy of Family Physicians

 


✨ BRING YOUR BEST CLINICAL WORK TO LEGION

If you are a thoughtful, evidence-based PMHNP who wants the flexibility of remote practice, meaningful clinical autonomy, robust operational support, and a community committed to excellent psychiatric care, we would be excited to learn more about you.

 


🤝 EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY

We encourage applicants from all backgrounds to apply.

Quality and patient experience are paramount to us. This means recruiting exceptional providers, championing evidence-based protocols, and displaying compassion in every patient interaction. Our exceptional PMHNPs operate with clinical autonomy, supported by experienced psychiatrists through consults and peer case reviews.

Our vision is to pioneer a new era of medicine by delivering world-class psychiatry. We believe in a future where every person can access the compassionate, high-quality care they need.

 

🚀 About the Role

Practice at the top of your license, from wherever you do your best work. This role is designed for PMHNPs who want meaningful clinical autonomy without having to build and operate a private practice alone.

We are looking for clinically excellent, patient-centered PMHNPs to provide psychiatric care through telehealth. Full-time and part-time positions are available.

 

💙 Benefits

Legion’s model is built to give clinicians more time for patients, fewer administrative distractions, and the support of a high-caliber psychiatric community.

  • Flexibility: Set your own schedule for optimal work-life balance.

  • Work from Home: See patients from the comfort of your home via telehealth.

  • Significant Administrative Support: You focus on patient care, and we’ll handle scheduling, insurance verification, billing, prior authorizations, pharmacy coordination, etc.

  • Patient Acquisition: Unlike with a private practice, we’ll work to fill your schedule, so you don’t have to do your own marketing.

  • Collaborating Physician Coverage: Where applicable, we provide your collaborating psychiatrist and fully cover the costs.

  • Competitive Pay: We compensate our providers at market-leading rates.

  • Weekly Pay: We pay our providers every week for immediate financial benefit and planning ease.

  • Legal Protection: We provide full malpractice insurance coverage.

  • Clinical Autonomy: We hire the most skilled providers and trust them to do what’s best for patients.

  • Technical Support: We cover the costs for you to have best-in-class EHR, e-Prescribe, and AI tools.

  • Credentialing Support: We handle all aspects and costs of credentialing with a large number of insurance plans, including commercial, ACA, and government, ensuring your legal and effective authorization within insurance networks.

  • Licensure and DEA Coverage: We’ll reimburse you for all fees associated with getting licensed in other states as required by Legion.

  • Commitment to Responsible Prescribing and High-Quality Care: We have rigorous, evidence-based protocols and provide objective diagnostic tools to ensure responsible and ethical prescriptions of controlled substances.

  • Community of Clinical Excellence: You will work alongside the most talented PMHNPs and psychiatrists in the world. Our current PMHNPs have trained at some of the country’s most prestigious institutions, including Vanderbilt, UT Austin, Johns Hopkins, Columbia, NYU, and UTHealth Houston.

  • Opportunities for Professional Growth: As we expand, we intend to promote clinical leadership from the best of our active providers.

  • Culture of Excellence through Innovation: Actively participate in ushering in a new era of mental health care through superior clinical care and technology.

  • Resources: We provide premium subscriptions to resources such as UpToDate and Carlat.

  • Exclusive Events: Engage with your colleagues through exclusive in-person and virtual events.

 

✅ Responsibilities

  • Provide excellent patient care for conditions including depression, anxiety, ADHD, insomnia, PTSD, bipolar disorder, etc.

  • Perform comprehensive psychiatric assessments, including mental-health history, medical history, diagnostic evaluation, and risk analysis.

  • Create and execute individualized treatment plans that may combine medication management and brief psychotherapy.

  • Provide compassionate, respectful, and patient-centered care.

  • Use evidence-based clinical protocols and responsible prescribing practices.

  • Collaborate with psychiatrists and clinical peers through consultations and case reviews.

  • Use technology and operational systems effectively to deliver reliable telehealth care.

 

🧰 Qualifications

  • Active, unrestricted state-issued authority to practice as a PMHNP in at least one U.S. state or jurisdiction.

  • Strong clinical assessment, diagnostic, and medication-management skills.

  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.

  • Comfort providing care remotely and using electronic health record systems.

  • Commitment to patient-centered, compassionate, evidence-based care.

 

📍 Role Logistics

  • Location: Fully remote within the United States.

  • Schedule: Full-time or part-time positions are available.

  • Compensation: $150K–$300K per year, depending on completed patient-care hours.

 

🤝 Clinical Advisory Board

Legion’s Clinical Advisory Board brings together nationally recognized psychiatrists, physician executives, telepsychiatry pioneers, and primary-care leaders. Working closely with Legion’s medical leadership, they help shape our clinical quality standards, evidence-based care protocols, prescribing safeguards, risk-management practices, and continuous quality-improvement efforts as the company scales.

Members of our Clinical Advisory Board include:

  • Madhukar Trivedi, M.D. — Psychiatrist; Professor of Psychiatry and Distinguished Chair in Mental Health at UT Southwestern

  • Alexander Ruvalcaba, M.D. — Psychiatrist; Physician Executive at MultiCare Behavioral Health Network

  • Jon Kole, M.D. — Psychiatrist; Senior Medical Director at Headspace

  • Liberty Eberly, D.O. — Psychiatrist; Co-Founder and Former Chief Medical Officer at innovaTel Telepsychiatry

  • John Lusins, M.D. — Psychiatrist; Founder and President at South Texas Mental Health Associates

  • Jacqueline Champlain, M.D. — Family Medicine Physician; Lead Physician at WellMed and Fellow of the American Academy of Family Physicians

 

✨ Bring Your Best Clinical Work to Legion

If you are a thoughtful, evidence-based PMHNP who wants the flexibility of remote practice, meaningful clinical autonomy, robust operational support, and a community committed to excellent psychiatric care, we would be excited to learn more about you.

 

🤝 Equal Employment Opportunity

Legion Health is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees, contractors, and applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or any other protected characteristic under applicable law. We encourage applicants from all backgrounds to apply.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
🧠 About Legion Health

At Legion Health, we believe everyone deserves fast, affordable, and world-class health care, and we’re developing the AI infrastructure to deliver it ourselves at world scale.

Legion is building autonomous medical care (the AI doctor), starting with psychiatry. Our AI-native care-delivery platform currently automates 95% of the administrative work required for us to deliver direct patient care. We also recently became the first company ever to receive regulatory authorization to let AI prescribe psychiatric medications, allowing us to not only collapse health care’s admin costs but also its clinical labor costs—shifting this industry’s economics from humans to tokens.

Our technical moat is hard to copy—we combine rich data, production AI, doctors in the loop, and end-to-end care operations to deliver measurably better care to a clinically complex patient population. This has helped us produce tens of thousands of total visits in just 2 years, all while holding ops costs flat and achieving industry-leading patient NPS and retention. While the last generation of healthcare startups made the existing system incrementally more efficient, Legion is rebuilding full-stack care delivery from first principles. Our vision? A 10X better patient experience that’s higher quality, less expensive, and more scalable than ever before. And a 10X better clinician experience that frees our providers to focus on what matters most: caring for patients.

Legion Health is backed by Y Combinator, leading venture capital firms, and founders from Function Health, Modern Health, Everly Health, Trusted Health, Clipboard Health, PatientPing, Sesame Care, Faire, EasyPost, and fuboTV.

Join us as we build the future of health care: faster, higher-quality, and more affordable, powered by doctors and AI working together.

 

🚀 The role

Hey, I'm Daniel G Wilson, co-founder and CTO at Legion. I studied applied math and CS at Princeton, led the Office Scripts and Power Automate integration at Microsoft, and did deep learning and RL research before that. GitHub: https://github.com/danielgwilson

I'm hiring a principal-level engineer to own the hardest systems in our care platform, whole. Not tickets, not a lane inside someone else's architecture: entire problem spaces, from "this is a mess" to "this is done and here's the doc."

Here's the honest shape of the job. We run a regulated clinical product (we e-prescribe controlled substances) on an event-driven TypeScript platform, and we ship at unusual velocity with heavy agent leverage. The engineers who have thrived here share one behavior: I hand them a gnarly domain, they disappear into it, and they come back with it working, documented, and theirs. I don’t need to check their work or meddle, because checking isn’t unnecessary. That’s the seat. The people who have struggled here waited for scoped tickets to tell them what to do—but that’s what we have agents for.

 

✅ What you'll own

Real domains, picked together in week one from this list, with written authority over them:

  • The factory spine. Own the question of how we get maximum leverage in the era of agentic engineering. We ship 500–1,000 PRs a month with a lean team. Merge gates, migration safety, canary and rollback on a system where a bad deploy can touch patient care—this all works today. Your job will be to move us towards 10,000 while maintaining quality and rigor.

  • The clinical work spine. Our event-sourced system of record for clinical work (orders, tasks, commands, receipts): the layer that lets AI agents and humans act on patient care with auditability and fail-closed checks. You’ll own the guardrails that ensure agents can safely provide broader and broader components of care.

  • Agent operations in production. LLM agents doing real clinical-adjacent work with tool use, checks, and receipts. You decide how autonomy expands and ratchets upwards as proof accumulates. Your agent harness will help prescribe psychiatric medication, legally, at the second company ever allowed to.

  • The data and metrics estate. Warehouse, analytics platform, and the pipelines that tell us what actually happened.

  • Architecture syncs with me. You'll have the standing I give someone who has seen more systems than I have: disagree with me, make the call in your domain, unpack it for the team when asked.

 

🏆 What "a fit" looks like, concretely

  • You've owned architecture across multiple companies or many codebases: staff-plus IC, chief-architect, or platform-consulting background. You've seen a dozen ways teams ship and you have opinions with scars behind them.

  • You ship daily at high volume with a fleet of AI agents. That’s table stakes. In the interview we'll ask to see your actual setup and what you let it do unsupervised. "I use Copilot sometimes" is not this.

  • When handed an ambiguous, ugly, load-bearing problem, your instinct is to take it whole: read everything, decide, build, write the doc, tell us what you decided. Not to schedule a meeting about scope.

  • You communicate proactively in writing. The pattern we love: a Sunday text that says "took care of it, here's the PR and what I changed."

  • You hold clinical-grade correctness without losing speed: auditability, HIPAA, fail-closed defaults, invariants over vibes.

This is a senior seat. Typically that means 10+ years and multiple systems owned end to end, but we care about the scars, not the number. We have separate openings for earlier-career engineers; this is not that. We need someone who’s seen some shit.

This role is not for you if you want to manage instead of build, you need well-scoped tickets to be productive, or big-company pace feels normal to you.

 

💻 Our Tech Stack

  • TypeScript, Node.js, Postgres, Next.js on Vercel, AWS, production LLM agent orchestration and bespoke harnesses, tools, CLIs, skills, evals and observability, EHR and e-prescribing integrations, PHI-grade security and audit trails.

 

📍 Role Logistics, Compensation, and Benefits

  • Job type: Full-time

  • Role type: Engineering

  • US Visa Sponsorship: Yes

  • Salary: $250,000 to $400,000 depending on experience, plus meaningful early-stage equity in a category defining company.

  • Health Insurance: Medical, dental, and vision benefits

  • Additional Perks: In-person retreats, meal stipends, etc.

  • Time Off: Flexible, unlimited vacation policy

  • Work hours: flexible but demanding—because we are (literally) saving lives.

  • Work Setup: In-person @ San Francisco HQ; partial remote considered for exceptional candidates (our track record includes both).

  • Impact: Work on something that truly matters to millions of patients and families.

  • Autonomy and Learning: Ownership over your projects with the freedom to set priorities, shape processes, and drive outcomes end-to-end.

  • Growth Opportunities: As we scale, we envision our top performers stepping into expanded roles and joining our executive leadership team.

 

🤝 Equal Employment Opportunity

Legion Health is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees, contractors, and applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or any other protected characteristic under applicable law. We encourage applicants from all backgrounds to apply.

jobs.title: Market Expansion & Clinician Operations Lead (backed by Y Combinator, $5M+ ARR, $23M+ raised)
jobs.descriptionHtml:
🧠 ABOUT LEGION HEALTH

At Legion Health, we believe everyone deserves fast, affordable, and world-class health care, and we’re developing the AI infrastructure to deliver it ourselves at world scale.

Legion is building autonomous medical care (the AI doctor), starting with psychiatry. Our AI-native care-delivery platform currently automates 95% of the administrative work required for us to deliver direct patient care. We also recently became the first company ever to receive regulatory authorization to let AI prescribe psychiatric medications, allowing us to not only collapse health care’s admin costs but also its clinical labor costs—shifting this industry’s economics from humans to tokens.

Our technical moat is hard to copy—we combine rich data, production AI, doctors in the loop, and end-to-end care operations to deliver measurably better care to a clinically complex patient population. This has helped us produce tens of thousands of total visits in just 2 years, all while holding ops costs flat and achieving industry-leading patient NPS and retention. While the last generation of healthcare startups made the existing system incrementally more efficient, Legion is rebuilding full-stack care delivery from first principles. Our vision? A 10X better patient experience that’s higher quality, less expensive, and more scalable than ever before. And a 10X better clinician experience that frees our providers to focus on what matters most: caring for patients.

Legion Health is backed by Y Combinator, leading venture capital firms, and founders from Function Health, Modern Health, Everly Health, Trusted Health, Clipboard Health, PatientPing, Sesame Care, Faire, EasyPost, and fuboTV.

Join us as we build the future of health care: faster, higher-quality, and more affordable, powered by doctors and AI working together.

📍 ROLE LOGISTICS

  • Job Type: Full-Time

  • Role Type: Market Expansion / Clinician Operations / Workforce Planning

  • Ideal Experience Level: 3+ years in healthcare operations or equivalent experience, including multi-market execution

  • Location: Onsite in San Francisco, CA

🚀 THE OPPORTUNITY

Legion is hiring a Market Expansion & Clinician Operations Lead to turn expansion plans into markets that are ready to deliver care, with the right clinician capacity in the right places. You will connect market prioritization, state-entry execution, workforce forecasting, recruiting, onboarding, and capacity deployment into one reliable operating process.

You will partner with Operations, Clinical, Revenue & Network Operations, Provider Partnerships, Finance, Product, and Engineering. Your job is to make dependencies and decision gates explicit, surface risks early, and ensure a launch becomes sustainable clinical capacity rather than a collection of completed checklists.

This is a hands-on operating leadership role. You should be comfortable building a forecast, working a launch's critical path, improving recruiting and onboarding workflows, and turning recurring manual work into measurable, repeatable systems. Clinical decisions remain with clinical leadership; legal, regulatory, and payer approvals remain with the relevant accountable experts.

✅ RESPONSIBILITIES AND DELIVERABLES

  • Build market-entry plans that connect demand, payer readiness, clinician supply, launch economics, operating capacity, and cross-functional dependencies.

  • Run launch readiness reviews with clear owners, milestones, evidence, risks, and decision gates; resolve critical-path blockers and escalate tradeoffs early.

  • Coordinate state entry and payer-entry readiness with Revenue & Network Operations and legal, compliance, and clinical partners; track required approvals without substituting for their judgment.

  • Forecast clinician demand and productive capacity by market, specialty, schedule, and expected patient demand; make hiring and deployment recommendations from that forecast.

  • Own the operating process from clinician recruiting through offer acceptance, onboarding, readiness, and productive deployment, in partnership with the recruiting and clinical teams.

  • Improve handoffs across licensing, credentialing, contracting, training, systems access, scheduling, and availability, so clinicians are ready when patients need them.

  • Create clear readiness standards and dashboards for offer-to-ready conversion, time to productive capacity, coverage gaps, and capacity utilization.

  • Partner with Finance and relevant operations owners on accurate clinician compensation administration and reconciliation.

  • Track launch performance through first visit, clean claim, and cash milestones with the teams accountable for each stage.

  • Document repeatable playbooks, improve workflows, and partner with Product and Engineering on automation that removes avoidable coordination work.

  • Build a dependable operating cadence that gives leadership a clear view of market readiness, clinician supply, blocked decisions, and the next action.

🏆 YOU’LL BE SUCCESSFUL IF YOU…

  • Launch markets with clear readiness evidence, accountable owners, and fewer avoidable critical-path delays.

  • Match productive clinician capacity to demand while keeping coverage gaps and unused capacity visible.

  • Shorten the path from accepted offer to ready, productive clinician without skipping quality or compliance requirements.

  • Give clinical, commercial, and operations leaders a forecast and status view they trust.

  • Build repeatable processes that improve as Legion grows and reduce the manual effort required for each additional market.

🧰 IDEAL BACKGROUND AND SKILLS

  • Experience owning healthcare operations, clinical workforce operations, network expansion, or a comparable multi-market operating function.

  • Evidence that you have personally taken a complex launch or operational program from planning through measurable results.

  • Strong workforce planning, analytical, and financial judgment; comfort building capacity models, operating dashboards, and clear decision memos.

  • Practical understanding of clinician recruiting, onboarding, licensing, credentialing, payer readiness, and the dependencies that determine when care can begin.

  • Ability to coordinate legal, compliance, clinical, finance, commercial, and technical partners while keeping decision rights and accountability clear.

  • A hands-on systems mindset: you improve the underlying process, document it, measure it, and automate where appropriate.

  • High ownership, honest escalation, strong follow-through, and comfort making progress with incomplete information.

  • Experience with psychiatry, telehealth, multi-state clinician networks, or a rapidly scaling care-delivery organization is especially useful.

💰 COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

  • Salary: $160,000 – $230,000 annual base salary, based on experience

  • Early-Stage Equity: Competitive

  • Health Insurance: Medical, dental, and vision benefits

  • Additional Perks: In-person retreats, meal stipends, learning stipend, and AI tooling budget

  • Time Off: Flexible, unlimited vacation policy

  • Work Setup: Full-time, onsite in San Francisco, CA

  • Impact: Turn national expansion into reliable access to care and productive clinician capacity.

  • Autonomy and Learning: Own your work end-to-end with close cross-functional and founder collaboration.

  • Growth Opportunities: Build the operating foundation for a growing multi-market care-delivery organization.

🤝 EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY

Legion Health is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees, contractors, and applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or any other protected characteristic under applicable law. We encourage applicants from all backgrounds to apply.

jobs.title: Remote Patient Access & Intake Medical Virtual Assistant (backed by Y Combinator, $5M+ ARR, $23M+ raised)
jobs.descriptionHtml:
🧠 About Legion Health

At Legion Health, we believe everyone deserves fast, affordable, and world-class health care, and we’re developing the AI infrastructure to deliver it ourselves at world scale.

Legion is building autonomous medical care, starting with psychiatry. Our AI-native care-delivery platform automates much of the administrative work required to deliver direct patient care, allowing our clinicians and patient-support teams to focus on the moments where human judgment and empathy matter most.

Our technical moat is hard to copy—we combine rich data, production AI, doctors in the loop, and end-to-end care operations to deliver measurably better care to a clinically complex patient population. This has helped us complete tens of thousands of visits in just two years while holding operations costs flat and achieving industry-leading patient NPS and retention.

While the last generation of healthcare startups made the existing system incrementally more efficient, Legion is rebuilding full-stack care delivery from first principles. Our vision is a 10X better patient experience that is higher quality, less expensive, and more scalable—and a 10X better clinician experience that frees providers to focus on what matters most: caring for patients.

Legion Health is backed by Y Combinator, leading venture capital firms, and founders from Function Health, Modern Health, Everly Health, Trusted Health, Clipboard Health, PatientPing, Sesame Care, Faire, EasyPost, and fuboTV.

Join us as we build the future of health care: faster, higher-quality, and more affordable, powered by clinicians, patient-support professionals, and AI working together.

📍 Role Logistics

  • Job Type: Contract

  • Role Type: Patient Access / Patient Intake / Patient Experience Operations

  • Ideal Experience Level: 2+ years

  • Location: Fully Remote

  • Work Hours: 8-hour shift between 6:00 AM and 10:00 PM Central Time

  • US Visa Sponsorship: No

🚀 The Opportunity

Legion is hiring a detail-oriented, healthcare-fluent Medical Virtual Assistant to support patients during the earliest and most important parts of their care journey.

You will help ensure that every prospective and newly booked patient is contacted quickly, welcomed warmly, prepared clearly, and routed correctly before their first visit. You will work across phone calls, patient messages, scheduling systems, intake documentation, insurance workflows, and internal coordination to prevent patients from becoming confused, delayed, or lost in the process.

This is not a traditional administrative-assistant role. You will be a frontline operator responsible for helping real patients navigate a complex healthcare experience. Patients may contact us when they are anxious, frustrated, missing documentation, experiencing scheduling problems, or unsure what to do next. You must be able to communicate calmly, clearly, accurately, and empathetically while keeping each patient moving toward care.

Excellent spoken and written English is essential. You will communicate directly with U.S.-based patients every day, document conversations for clinical and operations teams, and explain complicated logistical requirements in simple language without sounding robotic or dismissive.

We strongly prefer candidates with pharmacy, medical, nursing, behavioral-health, or other formal healthcare training outside the United States. This is a strictly non-clinical position: you will not diagnose patients, provide medical advice, recommend treatment, or practice under any medical or pharmacy license. Clinical fluency is valuable because it will help you understand patient needs, recognize sensitive issues, gather the right information, and escalate questions to the appropriate clinical team.

A meaningful part of the role may involve helping patients prepare for ADHD-related care. You should be comfortable learning detailed protocols, explaining documentation and release-of-information requirements, coordinating next steps, and helping patients feel prepared while remaining firmly within a non-clinical scope.

The right person is warm with patients, precise with documentation, reliable under pressure, and energized by the opportunity to improve the systems behind a rapidly growing mental-health practice.

✅ Responsibilities and Deliverables

  • Respond quickly to new leads and booked patients across phone, messaging, and internal systems.

  • Provide every patient with a warm, professional welcome and a clear explanation of what to expect before their first appointment.

  • Communicate with patients clearly, accurately, and empathetically in both spoken and written English.

  • Explain scheduling, intake, paperwork, insurance, and appointment-preparation requirements in simple, patient-friendly language.

  • Support appointment booking, rescheduling, intake completion, paperwork follow-up, and patient onboarding.

  • Monitor patients with incomplete intake forms, missing documentation, scheduling conflicts, insurance questions, pharmacy-related questions, or other barriers to care.

  • Manage patient-access workflows across self-service signups, referrals, Zocdoc leads, and other inbound channels.

  • Support ADHD-related intake preparation, including documentation requirements, release-of-information steps, and appointment expectations.

  • Help patients complete required logistical steps without providing clinical advice or making treatment recommendations.

  • Identify prescription, refill, prior-authorization, medication, safety, and clinical questions and escalate them promptly to the appropriate team.

  • Accurately document every material patient interaction so clinicians and teammates have complete, actionable context.

  • Maintain clear follow-up queues and ensure outstanding patient needs do not fall through the cracks.

  • Follow approved scripts, standard operating procedures, privacy requirements, and escalation protocols.

  • Partner closely with clinical, operations, billing, and patient-experience teams to resolve access barriers.

  • Maintain fast and consistent response times across assigned patient queues.

  • Identify recurring patient questions, delays, and workflow failures and share actionable feedback with operations, product, and clinical teams.

  • Help improve scripts, workflows, templates, and SOPs as Legion’s systems and care model evolve.

  • Maintain a reliable, high-speed internet connection and a quiet, professional environment for patient calls.

  • Protect patient privacy and handle sensitive information according to Legion’s policies and approved systems.

  • Consistently aim to deliver the best possible experience for patients and families.

🏆 You’ll Be Successful If You…

  • Make patients feel welcomed, respected, and supported from their first interaction with Legion.

  • Communicate clearly and confidently with patients by phone and in writing.

  • Explain next steps simply without sounding robotic, confusing, rushed, or dismissive.

  • Help more patients complete intake requirements and arrive prepared for their appointments.

  • Follow up consistently so patients do not become stuck or disappear because of preventable operational barriers.

  • Produce accurate, concise documentation that tells teammates exactly what happened and what needs to happen next.

  • Remain calm and professional when patients are worried, frustrated, delayed, or confused.

  • Recognize when a question is outside your scope and escalate it promptly to the correct clinical or operational owner.

  • Manage a high volume of patient conversations without losing important details or missing follow-ups.

  • Learn Legion’s care model, ADHD-related workflows, provider processes, scripts, and escalation paths quickly.

  • Use SOPs consistently while identifying opportunities to make patient-access workflows faster and more reliable.

  • Reduce avoidable manual work through strong organization, reusable documentation, and thoughtful process improvements.

  • Earn the trust of patients, clinicians, and teammates through reliability, sound judgment, and excellent follow-through.

🧰 Ideal Background and Skills

  • 2+ years of experience in healthcare operations, patient support, pharmacy support, medical administration, telehealth, healthcare call centers, or a similar role.

  • Exceptional spoken and written English communication skills.

  • Clear, warm, confident, and professional communication on patient phone calls.

  • Ability to explain detailed requirements in simple language while maintaining accuracy.

  • Strong patient-facing judgment, empathy, patience, and professionalism.

  • Excellent documentation skills and close attention to detail.

  • Strong organization and the ability to manage multiple active patient conversations and follow-up tasks.

  • Comfort working in a fast-paced startup where processes and responsibilities may evolve quickly.

  • Experience using systems such as Slack, Dialpad, Healthie, CRMs, EHRs, scheduling platforms, or similar tools.

  • Ability to work closely with clinical teams while respecting the boundaries of a non-clinical role.

  • Curiosity, initiative, and a willingness to learn the details of Legion’s care model and patient-access workflows.

  • Strong preference for candidates with formal healthcare education, training, or licensure outside the United States, including pharmacists, physicians, nurses, medical technologists, psychologists, or similar healthcare professionals.

  • Pharmacy experience is especially valuable, including familiarity with prescriptions, refills, prior authorizations, controlled-substance workflows, and medication-related patient questions.

  • Familiarity with behavioral health, psychiatry, ADHD care, telehealth, insurance, scheduling, referrals, or clinical documentation is strongly preferred.

  • Experience supporting U.S.-based patients or working within U.S. healthcare processes is a plus.

  • Availability to work consistently from 1:00 PM–9:30 PM Central Time.

  • A reliable computer, high-speed internet connection, professional call environment, and dependable remote-work setup.

The most important qualifications are patient empathy, excellent communication, healthcare fluency, operational execution, accurate documentation, and reliable follow-through.

⚕️ Non-Clinical Scope

This is a non-clinical patient-operations role.

  • You will not diagnose patients or assess medical conditions.

  • You will not provide medical or medication advice.

  • You will not recommend or make treatment decisions.

  • You will not interpret symptoms, laboratory results, or clinical records for patients.

  • You will not practice under a medical, nursing, pharmacy, or other healthcare license.

  • You will route clinical, medication, safety, and treatment questions to the appropriate licensed team member.

Your responsibility is to support patient logistics, documentation, scheduling, coordination, and escalation so patients can receive timely, high-quality care from the appropriate clinical team.

💰 Compensation & Benefits

  • Hourly Compensation: $5–$15 per hour, depending on experience

  • Work Hours: 8-hour shift between 6:00 AM and 10:00 PM Central Time

  • Work Setup: Fully remote

  • Impact: Help patients and families access mental-health care while contributing to a faster, more scalable healthcare system.

  • Autonomy and Learning: Develop deep experience across patient access, intake, telehealth operations, behavioral-health workflows, and AI-enabled care delivery.

  • Growth Opportunities: Take on increasing ownership across patient experience, access operations, workflow improvement, training, quality assurance, or team leadership as Legion scales.

🤝 Equal Employment Opportunity

Legion Health is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees, contractors, and applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or any other protected characteristic under applicable law. We encourage applicants from all backgrounds to apply.

The most important qualifications are patient empathy, excellent communication, healthcare fluency, operational execution, accurate documentation, and reliable follow-through.




⚕️ NON-CLINICAL SCOPE

This is a non-clinical patient-operations role.

 - You will not diagnose patients or assess medical conditions.

 - You will not provide medical or medication advice.

 - You will not recommend or make treatment decisions.

 - You will not interpret symptoms, laboratory results, or clinical records for patients.

 - You will not practice under a medical, nursing, pharmacy, or other healthcare license.

 - You will route clinical, medication, safety, and treatment questions to the appropriate licensed team member.

Your responsibility is to support patient logistics, documentation, scheduling, coordination, and escalation so patients can receive timely, high-quality care from the appropriate clinical team.




💰 COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

 - Hourly Compensation: $5–$15 per hour, depending on experience

 - Work Hours: 8-hour shift between 6:00 AM and 10:00 PM Central Time

 - Work Setup: Fully remote

 - Impact: Help patients and families access mental-health care while contributing to a faster, more scalable healthcare system.

 - Autonomy and Learning: Develop deep experience across patient access, intake, telehealth operations, behavioral-health workflows, and AI-enabled care delivery.

 - Growth Opportunities: Take on increasing ownership across patient experience, access operations, workflow improvement, training, quality assurance, or team leadership as Legion scales.

Join us as we build the future of health care: faster, higher-quality, and more affordable, powered by doctors and AI working together.

📍 ROLE LOGISTICS

  • Job Type: Full-Time

  • Role Type: Sales Enablement / Onboarding / Field Training / Provider Partnerships

  • Ideal Experience Level: 4+ years in sales enablement, sales training, or a closely related role

  • Location: Onsite in San Francisco, CA

  • Travel: Periodic field visits to support coaching and learning, aiming for 2–3 field days per month when feasible

🚀 THE OPPORTUNITY

Legion is hiring a Sales Enablement Lead to build the training and readiness system behind our provider-partnership team. You will help Provider Partnership Managers and Regional Managers learn the market, tell Legion's story accurately, execute the field motion, and build productive relationships with referring care teams.

Your first priority is new-hire onboarding: a focused one-to-two-week program with clear certification standards, practical rehearsal, and a strong bridge into the field. As hiring scales, you will build a repeatable cohort cadence, with onboarding during the first two weeks of the month and ongoing preboarding, coaching support, and curriculum improvement.

You will partner closely with Provider Partnerships leadership, Regional Managers, Revenue Operations, and clinical and operations experts. Enablement owns readiness, training, and learning systems. Regional Managers retain day-to-day rep performance management, while Revenue Operations owns commercial systems and planning.

✅ RESPONSIBILITIES AND DELIVERABLES

  • Build and run onboarding for Provider Partnership Managers and Regional Managers, including preboarding, live instruction, practice, certification, remediation, and the transition to field execution.

  • Translate the approved provider-partnership motion into clear playbooks for account preparation, outreach, discovery, referral workflows, follow-up, and relationship development.

  • Develop messaging, objection-handling guides, role plays, call examples, and field tools that help reps communicate clearly and accurately.

  • Partner with clinical, compliance, and operations leaders to keep clinical claims, referral guidance, policies, and patient-access messaging accurate and approved.

  • Train the team on CRM hygiene, workflow execution, handoffs, and reporting in partnership with Revenue Operations.

  • Equip Regional Managers with coaching frameworks, observation rubrics, reinforcement plans, and tools for developing their teams.

  • Spend time with the field team, observe real interactions, and turn frontline feedback into specific curriculum and playbook improvements.

  • Create a practical content library with clear ownership, version control, and a process for retiring outdated materials.

  • Support launches and process changes with training, communication, reinforcement, and measurement of adoption.

  • Measure onboarding completion, certification, remediation, productive ramp, time to first qualified referral, and workflow adoption with the relevant functional owners.

  • Use AI and modern learning tools to improve content production and practice while keeping materials accurate, useful, and grounded in the field.

🏆 YOU’LL BE SUCCESSFUL IF YOU…

  • New hires finish onboarding with demonstrated readiness and a clear plan for their first weeks in the field.

  • Reps and managers use the playbooks and coaching tools because they help them execute, not just because training was assigned.

  • Reduce avoidable ramp friction and improve time to productive provider relationships and qualified referrals.

  • Keep the team aligned as messaging, workflows, markets, and operating requirements change.

  • Create a steady feedback loop between the field, leadership, and training so each cohort is better prepared than the last.

🧰 IDEAL BACKGROUND AND SKILLS

  • Experience building and delivering sales onboarding or enablement programs, ideally for a growing field-sales or provider-partnership team.

  • Strong live facilitation, instructional design, coaching, and concise writing skills.

  • Evidence of improved readiness, ramp, adoption, or field execution from programs you personally owned.

  • Ability to turn complex product, clinical, operational, and commercial information into practical learning materials.

  • Comfort with CRM workflows, learning/content tools, performance data, and field observation.

  • Ability to distinguish a knowledge gap, a skill gap, a process problem, and a management issue, then work with the right owner.

  • A hands-on builder's approach: write the playbook, run the session, observe the field, measure the result, and improve it.

  • Healthcare, provider referrals, medical sales, or relationship-driven field-sales experience is a strong plus.

  • High ownership, low ego, clear communication, and willingness to travel periodically to learn from and support the field.

💰 COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

  • Salary: $120,000 – $170,000 annual base salary, based on experience

  • Early-Stage Equity: Competitive

  • Health Insurance: Medical, dental, and vision benefits

  • Additional Perks: In-person retreats, meal stipends, learning stipend, and AI tooling budget

  • Time Off: Flexible, unlimited vacation policy

  • Work Setup: Full-time, onsite in San Francisco, CA

  • Impact: Help provider-partnership teams bring more patients into high-quality care through accurate, consistent execution.

  • Autonomy and Learning: Own your work end-to-end with close cross-functional and founder collaboration.

  • Growth Opportunities: Build and scale Legion's enablement function as the provider-partnership organization grows.

🤝 EQUAL EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITY

Legion Health is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees, contractors, and applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or any other protected characteristic under applicable law. We encourage applicants from all backgrounds to apply.

jobs.descriptionHtml:
🧠 About Legion Health

At Legion Health, we believe everyone deserves fast, affordable, and world-class health care, and we’re developing the AI infrastructure to deliver it ourselves at world scale.

Legion is building autonomous medical care (the AI doctor), starting with psychiatry. Our AI-native care-delivery platform currently automates 95% of the administrative work required for us to deliver direct patient care. We also recently became the first company ever to receive regulatory authorization to let AI prescribe psychiatric medications, allowing us to not only collapse health care’s admin costs but also its clinical labor costs—shifting this industry’s economics from humans to tokens.

Our technical moat is hard to copy—we combine rich data, production AI, doctors in the loop, and end-to-end care operations to deliver measurably better care to a clinically complex patient population. This has helped us produce tens of thousands of total visits in just 2 years, all while holding ops costs flat and achieving industry-leading patient NPS and retention. While the last generation of healthcare startups made the existing system incrementally more efficient, Legion is rebuilding full-stack care delivery from first principles. Our vision? A 10X better patient experience that’s higher quality, less expensive, and more scalable than ever before. And a 10X better clinician experience that frees our providers to focus on what matters most: caring for patients.

Legion Health is backed by Y Combinator, leading venture capital firms, and founders from Function Health, Modern Health, Everly Health, Trusted Health, Clipboard Health, PatientPing, Sesame Care, Faire, EasyPost, and fuboTV.

Join us as we build the future of health care: faster, higher-quality, and more affordable, powered by doctors and AI working together.

📍 Role Logistics

  • Job Type: Full-Time

  • Role Type: Product / Technical Product Management / Consumer AI / Patient Experience / Retention

  • Ideal Experience Level: 5+ years

  • Location: San Francisco

  • US Visa Sponsorship: Yes

🚀 The Opportunity

Legion is hiring a Head of Product to own the consumer product experience that turns AI-native care delivery into something patients can understand, trust, use, and return to.

This is not a technical program management role, an enterprise roadmap coordinator role, or a “growth PM” role with healthcare language added on top. You will own real product surface area across Legion’s patient journey: onboarding, intake, eligibility, scheduling, visit prep, provider matching, care-plan clarity, medication workflows, follow-up, renewals, messaging, reactivation, and the moments that make a patient feel safe enough to come back.

The right person is technical enough to reason through APIs, data models, event instrumentation, AI workflows, edge cases, system constraints, and engineering tradeoffs, but consumer-minded enough to know that the best product often feels obvious, calm, and human. You should be able to sit with a patient problem, map the underlying clinical and operational workflow, write a crisp product spec, prototype the interaction, instrument the funnel, partner deeply with engineering and design, ship the feature, and decide whether it actually improved care.

Legion is a modern consumer AI software company that happens to deliver medical care. That means the product bar is closer to Anthropic, OpenAI, Character.AI, Replit, Oura, WHOOP, Duolingo, Chime, Monarch, and the best consumer health companies than to traditional healthcare software. We need someone who can bring that level of product taste, technical speed, and retention thinking into a regulated, high-trust category where quality and safety matter.

This is a high-ownership IC role with founder-level visibility and a direct path to management of a large product organization. You will work directly with engineering, design, clinical, operations, growth, data, compliance, and the founders to turn messy real-world care delivery into simple, powerful product experiences.

✅ Responsibilities and Deliverables

  • Own core patient-facing product surfaces across the full consumer journey: discovery, onboarding, intake, insurance/payment clarity, scheduling, provider fit, visit prep, visit completion, follow-up, care-plan adherence, refills, renewals, messaging, support, retention, and reactivation.

  • Translate complex clinical, operational, regulatory, and AI workflows into simple consumer experiences that reduce anxiety, increase clarity, and help patients know exactly what to do next.

  • Build durable product systems, not one-off features: patient timeline, care status, tasking, reminders, notifications, escalation paths, asynchronous messaging, support deflection, eligibility logic, provider availability, and follow-up workflows.

  • Partner with engineering to scope and ship technically sound products across web, mobile-responsive experiences, backend workflows, APIs, third-party integrations, event pipelines, data models, and AI-assisted workflows.

  • Define and own product metrics for your surface area, including activation, intake completion, scheduling conversion, first-visit completion, time to care, repeat-visit rate, renewal completion, retention, NPS/CSAT, patient confusion, support burden, no-shows, and ops cost per visit.

  • Use PostHog, SQL, analytics tools, customer support data, operational dashboards, and qualitative research to identify patient friction, prioritize product bets, and measure whether shipped work moved the right metrics.

  • Design and run structured experiments where appropriate, while knowing when a healthcare product needs principled product judgment, clinical input, and quality thresholds instead of pure A/B testing.

  • Own product specs, user stories, acceptance criteria, rollout plans, QA checklists, experiment plans, metric definitions, launch notes, and post-launch readouts with enough clarity that engineering, clinical, ops, and growth can all execute cleanly.

  • Prototype quickly using Figma, v0, Lovable, Replit, Cursor, Codex, Claude Code, lightweight scripts, no-code tools, or whatever helps you make product ideas concrete before engineering invests real cycles.

  • Ship production PRs regularly. This is a product role—not a software-engineering role—but you are expected to work directly in the codebase and open production-quality PRs for well-scoped changes such as instrumentation, internal tools, workflow logic, UI and copy improvements, prototypes, and small fixes. You should be comfortable testing, reviewing, and safely rolling out your work in close partnership with engineering.

  • Partner with clinical and operations teams to deeply understand real patient and provider workflows, including edge cases: missed appointments, medication refill timing, insurance confusion, state/provider availability, pharmacies, clinical escalations, patient safety concerns, handoffs, and support loops.

  • Partner with compliance, legal, privacy, and clinical leadership to design AI-enabled product experiences with appropriate safeguards, human review, auditability, expectation-setting, and patient trust.

  • Improve Legion’s AI product layer: patient-facing AI interactions, AI-assisted intake, personalization, care navigation, workflow automation, internal copilots, clinical/ops review queues, and evaluation loops that make automation safer and more useful over time.

  • Create product feedback loops from patient conversations, support tickets, provider feedback, drop-off data, session recordings, funnel analytics, and clinical/ops metrics so the roadmap is grounded in real behavior, not vibes.

  • Work with growth and brand to ensure acquisition promises match the actual product experience, so the patients we bring in understand what Legion does, feel properly oriented, and are more likely to stay in care.

  • Raise the product craft bar across Legion: clearer flows, better defaults, fewer dead ends, tighter copy, sharper state handling, cleaner mobile experiences, stronger instrumentation, faster iteration, and more rigorous launch quality.

🏆 You’ll Be Successful If You…

  • Make Legion’s patient experience feel consumer-grade: fast, clear, calm, trustworthy, and easy to return to.

  • Improve the core retention loop of care: more patients complete intake, make it to their first visit, understand the next step, follow through on care plans, complete renewals when eligible, and come back when they need help.

  • Turn messy clinical and operational workflows into product systems that scale without making patients feel like they are navigating a maze.

  • Ship AI-enabled experiences that feel useful and safe, with clear boundaries around what AI does, what doctors do, and when humans review or intervene.

  • Build a measurement system that makes the patient journey legible: every meaningful step has an owner, a metric, and a path to improvement.

  • Reduce patient confusion and support burden by improving the product itself, not just by adding more manual operations.

  • Help Legion move faster without becoming sloppy: strong specs, smart scoping, crisp decisions, high-quality launches, and honest post-launch learning.

  • Earn trust from engineering because you understand technical constraints and tradeoffs, and from clinical/ops teams because you understand the reality of care delivery.

  • Create product experiences that are emotionally intelligent without being soft, technically sophisticated without being confusing, and ambitious without being reckless.

  • Help build the product foundation for a company that can deliver world-class medical care at dramatically lower cost.

🧰 Ideal Background and Skills

  • 5+ years of product management, product engineering, technical founder, or equivalent experience, with meaningful ownership of consumer-facing web or mobile products.

  • Strong consumer product instincts. You have shipped products that people actually use, understand, trust, and return to, not just internal tools or enterprise workflows.

  • Technical fluency across software product development. You can reason through APIs, data models, event instrumentation, backend workflows, frontend states, AI workflows, latency, failure modes, privacy constraints, and engineering tradeoffs.

  • Hands-on technical curiosity. You can navigate API docs, logs, event payloads, session recordings, agent traces, and enough of a codebase to understand what is really happening without pulling engineers into every first-pass investigation.

  • Experience partnering deeply with engineering and design from problem definition through launch: discovery, PRDs/specs, UX flows, technical scoping, sprint planning, QA, rollout, metric tracking, and iteration.

  • Strong analytical ability. You are comfortable with SQL or equivalent data exploration, product analytics tools such as PostHog, Amplitude, Mixpanel, Looker, Hex, or Mode, and you can define useful metrics without waiting for someone else to hand you a dashboard.

  • Track record improving engagement, retention, activation, conversion, habit formation, lifecycle, or core experience metrics in a consumer product.

  • High product taste and UX judgment. You care about copy, information architecture, interaction design, empty states, error states, mobile responsiveness, notification timing, trust cues, and the emotional texture of the user experience.

  • AI-native working style. You already use tools like Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Replit, Lovable, v0, ChatGPT, Claude, Figma AI, or similar tools to prototype, analyze, write, synthesize, debug, and move faster.

  • Comfort working on AI-enabled products where the PM must think about prompt behavior, user expectations, evaluation, quality thresholds, fallback paths, human review, auditability, and safety.

  • Healthcare experience is a strong plus but not required. Experience in another trust-sensitive consumer category such as fintech, insurance, family/kids, identity, privacy, marketplaces, wellness, or regulated consumer products is also valuable.

  • Startup operating mode: high agency, low ego, high urgency, strong writing, strong judgment, strong follow-through. You can create clarity without waiting for a perfect org chart.

  • Ability to work cross-functionally with clinical, operations, support, compliance, legal, growth, data, design, engineering, and founders without losing the thread of the user problem.

  • Excellent writing. You can write crisp strategy docs, product specs, launch plans, decision memos, patient-facing copy, and post-launch analyses.

  • Bias toward building. You are happiest when you are close to the product, close to users, close to the data, and shipping.

  • Bonus: experience at or near companies like Anthropic, OpenAI, Character.AI, Replit, Cursor, Perplexity, Notion, Duolingo, Oura, WHOOP, Chime, Monarch Money, Rocket Money, Acorns, Function Health, Nourish, General Medicine, Circle Medical, Tava Health, Headway, Rula, Midi Health, Evvy, Ro, Hims & Hers, Thirty Madison, Levels, Superpower, or another breakout consumer product with high craft, high trust, and fast iteration.

💰 Compensation & Benefits

  • Salary: $190,000 – $330,000

  • Early-Stage Equity: Meaningful ownership in a category-defining company.

  • Health Insurance: Medical, dental, and vision benefits

  • Additional Perks: In-person retreats, meal stipends, AI/product tooling budget, learning stipend, home office support

  • Time Off: Flexible, unlimited vacation policy

  • Work Hours: Flexible

  • Work Setup: In-person in San Francisco

  • Impact: Build the product layer for a company trying to change health care forever.

  • Autonomy and Learning: Own major patient-facing product surfaces end-to-end, from product strategy through technical scoping, launch, measurement, and iteration.

  • Growth Opportunities: As we scale, this role can grow into Chief Product Officer.

📝 How to Apply and Hiring Process

  • Apply here: https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/legionhealth/0ffded39-1242-4a35-9bc3-0e5b0ce22276

  • Overview of our hiring process:

    1. Resume + Application Screen

    2. Founder / Product Interview

    3. Technical Product Deep Dive

    4. Cross-Functional Interviews with Engineering, Design, Clinical/Ops, Growth, and Founders

    5. Professional Reference Checks

  • Estimated time-to-hire: 2 weeks

  • Start date: ASAP

  • Hiring manager: Arthur MacWaters

🤝 Equal Employment Opportunity

Legion Health is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees, contractors, and applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or any other protected characteristic under applicable law. We encourage applicants from all backgrounds to apply.
